About This Job
About the role
We’re looking for a strong Senior Software engineer with a passion for robotics to help deliver reliable software for our cell therapy manufacturing platform. You’ll spend your time designing, building, testing and improving software, from interfaces with integrated mobile robots and low-level factory control to factory operation, automation and orchestration.
You’ll work within the robotics team and closely with colleagues across software and systems engineering teams to turn requirements into working solutions. You’ll contribute to technical design and help resolve delivery challenges, while mentoring other engineers and promoting high-quality software.
This is a hands-on role. You’ll regularly deploy software onto physical systems, run integration tests with robots and connected bioprocess equipment, and investigate issues at the boundary between software and hardware. Professional robotics experience is welcome, but is not required: we’re interested in your software engineering skills, curiosity and enthusiasm for learning.
What you’ll do
•
Take technical ownership of the design, architecture, implementation and debugging of maintainable software components, services and interfaces across the robotics platform, driving key architectural decisions and ensuring solutions are scalable, robust and aligned with long-term platform objectives.
•
Integrate software with robots, devices and equipment.
•
Develop and run tests on hardware to verify behaviour, diagnose failures and check fixes under realistic operating conditions.
•
Build quality into delivery through test-driven development, automated testing, continuous integration, and code review.
•
Mentor colleagues, share technical knowledge and help junior engineers deliver consistent, high-quality software.
•
Collaborate across disciplines to resolve integration issues and deliver working features at a sustainable pace.
•
Maintain clear technical documentation and test evidence to support development, verification and regulatory requirements.

Qualifications
What you’ll bring
•
Significant experience delivering complex software, with strong skills in design, implementation, testing and debugging across the development lifecycle.
•
High proficiency in Python programming.
•
Strong understanding of object-oriented programming and software design patterns, with experience building backend services or applications and integrating systems through APIs or messaging.
•
Experience with distributed systems using message-oriented or event-based approaches.
•
Good engineering habits, including version control, automated testing and continuous integration.
•
The ability to mentor other engineers, explain technical ideas clearly and collaborate with colleagues across disciplines.
•
A genuine interest in robotics and the willingness to work hands-on with hardware, learning how to test and troubleshoot integrated systems.
Desirable skills
These are useful additions, rather than requirements. Robotics experience can come from personal projects, study, research or professional work.
•
Robotics or automation experience, including ROS or ROS 2, mobile robots, robotic arms, motion control or machine vision.
•
Experience integrating software with hardware, low-level peripherals or industrial communication protocols such as MQTT.
•
Experience with factory control, automation, orchestration or safety-relevant software.
•
Front-end development, for example using TypeScript or JavaScript with a web framework.
•
Experience with virtualisation, containers, cloud services or IoT integration using GCP, Azure or AWS.
•
Experience developing software in medical or biotechnology settings, including verification, traceability and regulatory documentation.

Additional Information
Cellular Origins is currently based on the TTP Campus, within purpose-built sustainable offices, labs and green surroundings, 10 miles south of Cambridge.  Our working culture encourages entrepreneurship, shared ideas and collaboration, while providing you the freedom to do your best work.
Our employee benefits include:
• Annual bonus
• 25 days holiday
• Employer pension contribution of 10% of salary
• Private medical insurance for employees and dependants
• Enhanced family friendly leave
• Life insurance worth 6x salary
• Electric car leasing scheme
• Cycle to work scheme
• Season ticket loan

• AI-enabled engineering: GenAI-assisted development, agentic workflows and appropriate engineering, security and governance controls.

• You have designed and delivered modern data platforms that are scalable, reliable and cost-effective in enterprise environments.
• Making sound architectural decisions across ingestion, storage, processing, modelling, orchestration and serving.

• Making pragmatic technology choices and understanding the trade-offs between platform, storage, processing and integration patterns.
• You shape the end-to-end engineering lifecycle, improving how teams build, test, deploy and operate software and data products.

About This Job
At Home Instead we have minimum 1-hour calls plus suitable travel time to ensure you are not rushed with clients, with mileage reimbursement. We work to match our Care Professionals and clients together so memorable connections can be established. All initial calls with a client who is new to you will be introductions with the support of another colleague, so you can really get to know your client and their needs.
Responsibilities as a Domiciliary Support Worker:
• Offering warmth and care during evening visits.
• Enhance the home atmosphere by aiding in light household chores and meal preparations.
• Help clients cherish their time with you, sharing in activities such as reading or watching favourite TV shows.
• Support with personal care tasks such as showering, washing hair, and getting changed.
• Taking clients out to places of their choice e.g. the local shops.
• Ensure transparent communication with clients and loved ones, offering first-rate care and comfort.
Requirements:
• Experience is not required; we offer comprehensive in-house training. However, any previous care experience either professional or personal is an advantage.
• You must have a full driver's licence and dependable transportation for various duties.
• You must have flexibility and be able to work alternate weekends.
• You must be reliable and punctual to ensure we can continue to provide an excellent service to our clients.
• Must have a caring, friendly disposition to create lasting relationships.
• Must live in or very close to Leek to be a suitable match for our Leek-based clients.
£12.50 - £13.50 per hour

Being a care Professional is a highly rewarding career where no two days are the same! With minimum 1 hour care visits and client matching, you have the time to provide high quality, person-focused care.
If you’re looking for a profession where you can bring your caring personality to work and change lives, look no further. We’re looking for Care Professionals who have access to reliable transportation as some of our clients can live in remote areas and require accompanying to Doctor's visits.

Qualifications
Due to the nature of this role, candidates must hold a valid driver’s license and have access to a suitable vehicle for travel to and from client locations.

About This Job
We’re looking for Care Professionals who are kind and compassionate and who, by understanding our values and our mission, are dedicated to delivering the highest standard of care. To ensure continuity for both Clients and Care Professionals, you will see the same Clients every week, with minimum one hour visits, enabling you to build a relationship and a routine focused around quality of life in the comfort of the Client’s home.
Home Care is care carried out in an older adult’s own home, rather than in another setting like a hospital, assisted living facility, care home or nursing home. If the person needs specific medical care it may be recommended that they move to one of these facilities, but most types of care – including complex care, dementia care, palliative care and more – can take place in the home. Home carers can assist with daily living activities in a safe manner while the older person remains in the comfort and familiarity of their own home where they can retain some or most of their independence. Care Professionals can help with tasks such as:
• Personal care (such as getting to the bathroom and getting dressed
• Helping clients get to the bathroom during the night
• Providing medication reminders, and administering this if relevant
• Encouraging the person to eat nutritious meals
• Providing meal preparation and cooking, while adhering to any dietary requirements
• Helping with regular housework and other chores
• Helping clients with mobility issues to move around safely in the home
• Driving clients to weekly appointments
• Offering regular companionship and observing their mental health
• Organising enjoyable and stimulating activities for the client
The home environment is a key part of maintaining dignity in care for older adults, more so than other settings. Studies have found those receiving care in other settings, such as a hospital, experienced mild to severe loss of dignity. For this reason, helping an older adult to remain in their own home could drastically improve their care experience.

Qualifications
There’s nothing more powerful than the ability to change somebody’s life for the better every day, whether that’s simply keeping them company, or offering more advanced personal or dementia care. And we’ll give you all the training you need to confidently make the role your own. As a Care Professional, you can make a world of difference to people’s lives the minute you step through your client’s door, helping them to live independently, at home, with exceptional care. About This Job
We’ve built a global platform that moves money across borders instantly, transparently, and at the lowest possible cost. As we continue to scale our operations and expand our capabilities in the UK, the size and complexity of our balance sheet, safeguarding structures, and liquid asset pools are growing.
We are looking for a Treasury Manager – ALM to join our Group Treasury team. In this role, you will take ownership of liquidity management, balance sheet risk oversight, and compliance for our core UK asset portfolios and liquid buffers. Operating with a high degree of autonomy as a key ALM partner, you will drive first-line risk oversight while seamlessly leveraging the robust infrastructure and shared resources of our wider global Treasury function.
Your mission is to ensure our UK portfolios maintain institutional-grade financial resilience. Working alongside our Treasury leadership, you will be responsible for the day-to-day risk management of our high-quality liquid asset buffers, monitoring structural balance sheet exposures (IR, FX, and Credit), and ensuring our funding and liquidity strategies are fully aligned with evolving UK industry and regulatory expectations.
Here’s what you’ll be doing
• Portfolio & Compliance Monitoring: Oversee the compliance, monitoring, and risk management of the UK liquid asset buffers, ensuring strict adherence to internal liquidity policies and safeguarding risk frameworks.
• Evolution to Strategy: While the initial focus is on robust risk oversight and monitoring, you will actively collaborate on and evolve the long-term investment strategy and asset allocation for these portfolios as our UK footprint grows.
• Balance Sheet Risk Management: Act as the first line of defense for the portfolio’s financial risks. You will identify, measure, and monitor structural interest rate risk and Foreign Exchange (FX) exposures to safeguard the balance sheet.
• Funding & Intragroup Arrangements: Manage regional funding requirements, including the oversight of intragroup funding arrangements (term and intraday), capital optimisation, and cash forecasting.
• Regulatory Alignment: Ensure regional treasury operations meet all UK liquidity and capital preservation expectations (leveraging your experience with liquidity stress testing and capital adequacy frameworks).
• Group Collaboration: Act as the primary bridge between the UK business and our global Treasury execution desk, translating portfolio risk management and ALM needs into actionable requirements.
This role will suit you if you have
• A Regulated Treasury Background: You have strong experience working within a UK-regulated financial institution (such as a sophisticated capital-regulated FinTech/EMI, investment firm, building society, or regulated bank).
• Liquid Asset & Portfolio Expertise: You possess a deep understanding of liquid asset buffers, liquidity metrics, and the nuances of managing high-quality fixed income portfolios.
• Asset-Liability Management (ALM) Grip: You are comfortable identifying and monitoring structural balance sheet risks. Strong familiarity with ALM principles, interest rate risk management, and balance sheet dynamics is essential.
• Regulatory Fluency: You are familiar with UK regulatory liquidity expectations, capital requirements, and stress testing processes (e.g., ICARA or ILAAP/ICAAP concepts).

The Details

• Own and continuously improve the financial control environment for Technology expenditure, including the appropriate treatment of operating and capital expenditure.
• Translate complex financial information into concise, decision-focused insight for Technology leaders, Finance leadership and executive forums.
• Improve the quality, accessibility and efficiency of reporting, using Power BI, planning tools and automation to reduce manual activity and enable greater self-service.
• Lead, coach and develop colleagues supporting the Technology cost base, setting clear standards for ownership, accuracy, stakeholder management and proactive problem-solving.
• Support our culture by championing Diversity, Equity & Inclusion strategies.

About This Job
We are recruiting for a Head of PR and Corporate Communications to join our Marketing department.
The Head of PR & Corporate Communications is responsible for shaping, protecting and promoting Worcester Bosch. This role leads all external communications, including media relations, corporate messaging, Thought Leadership, issues management and crisis communications, ensuring consistent and compelling storytelling across all channels.
The role partners closely with senior leadership to align communications with business strategy, supporting growth objectives and building trust with key stakeholders. The successful candidate will lead the development and execution of a comprehensive PR and corporate communications strategy aligned to business goals. They will also lead, mentor and develop the in-house PR team and nurture the relationship with our external PR agency.
Marketing PR responsibilities include:
• Leading the strategic planning for PR, identifying and delivering initiatives as part of the annual PR plan.
• Managing the overall PR budget, ensuring strong ROI and effectiveness by setting clear objectives and KPIs.
• Working with our PR agency to build and maintain strong media relationships that secure high-quality, proactive coverage across national, trade and international outlets.
• Preparing key spokespeople for media engagements, with the potential to also be a spokesperson.
• Tracking performance against KPIs.
Corporate Communications responsibilities include:
• Working with the Executive Team and HR Director to develop and deploy our Corporate Communications plan.
• Collaborating with Internal Communications and People teams to ensure alignment between internal and external messaging.
• Acting as a senior communications advisor to the executive team, supporting with corporate announcements.
• Leading reputation management, including issues and crisis communications planning and response.
• Preparing key spokespeople for media engagements.
This is a leadership role and the incumbent is expected to lead by example, demonstrating strong, visible leadership across the Marketing function and the wider business, setting standards for collaboration, accountability and performance. We are looking for someone who has strong influencing skills, possesses sound judgement and demonstrates high levels of discretion. To be successful you’ll need to be calm and confident under pressure, highly organised with strong attention to detail, proactive, solutions-focused and resilient.
It is essential that you have significant experience in PR, corporate communications, or reputation management. We’ll want to see your proven track record of delivering high-impact media coverage and corporate campaigns, as well as strong experience advising senior executives and managing high-profile issues. You will be media trained and have excellent written and verbal communication skills. We are looking for a strategic thinker with strong commercial awareness and who has plenty of experience managing agencies and cross-functional stakeholders
If you think this is you, please send us your CV and a covering letter explaining why you are great fit for the role.

Degree in Public Relations, Communications, Journalism, Marketing or related discipline.

• Credible, calm and confident under pressure
• Highly organised with strong attention to detail
• Proactive, solutions-focused and resilient

Essential Experience

About This Job
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.
Hello, hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!
Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.
Where and how you can work
The buzzing Canva London campus features several buildings around beautiful leafy Hoxton Square in Shoreditch. While our global headquarters is in Sydney, Australia, London is our HQ for Europe, with all kinds of teams based here, plus event spaces to gather our team and communities. You’ll experience a warm welcome from our Vibe team at front of house, amazing home cooked food from our Head Chef and a variety of workspaces to hang out with your team mates or get solo work done. That said, we trust our Canvanauts to choose the balance that empowers them and their team to achieve their goals and so you have choice in where and how you work.
About the Team
The Localisation group is responsible for the localisation of Canva’s product, marketing, and content as well as the tools, processes, and assets that make this possible. We sit within the International Supergroup but we work closely with stakeholders in Growth and across the whole organisation. Our mission is to celebrate the diversity of our global users and make their interactions with Canva delightful by delivering a hyperlocalised experience.
You will be part of a small but powerful UK team and there will be lots of opportunities to collaborate with many other specialities beyond localisation so we value energy and adaptability over specific experience or years of experience.
About the Role
Every month, more than 100 million Canva users create a design in one of the 100 languages other than English, that Canva supports. The Localisation specialty is a small team of linguists, project managers, and engineers distributed throughout the company.
As a Product, Localisation and Growth Partner for the UK, you'll bring your product experience, cultural knowledge to all aspects of Canva for UK users, ensuring our users have the best possible Canva experience.
You will be the voice of UK users and the champion for culturally relevant content. Ultimately, you’ll be leading the charge in Empowering UK to Design!
What you’ll do
•
Identify key opportunities for localisation improvements for the UK market
•
Identify and fix product funnel problems through signups, authentication, all the way to editing and publishing
•
Collaborate with the UK team on Product Growth initiatives
•
Tailor content for the nuances of the UK market
•
Evaluate and adapt global messaging, campaigns, and product experiences to resonate with UK users
•
Provide cultural insights and guidance to global teams to produce content that suits UK audiences
•
Work closely with local partners to ensure clarity, tone, and cultural nuance across all surfaces
•
Partner with internal stakeholders to develop language style guides, tone of voice strategies and localisation best practices
What we're looking for
You understand the needs of UK customers and the opportunities to meet those needs effectively.
You have proven product management experience, including owning product strategy and working in cross-functional teams.
We’re also looking for someone with tertiary experience in conversion rate optimisation seeing as the job entails improving the success rates across all of our landing pages and user workflows for the UK user.
We’re open to candidates from a range of backgrounds, and valuable experience could include product, growth, localisation or internationalisation work, and/or content design. Previous experience working for a SaaS or technology company is also highly valued.
You’re passionate about language and culture and you understand how these can impact local users’ experience of a product. Above all else, you care deeply about creating experiences that feel natural and intuitive so that Canva resonates with UK users and feels like home for them. Your analytical mindset helps you evaluate campaign effectiveness and recommend data-driven improvements for optimising user experiences.
You thrive in flat, collaborative environments where ideas can come from anywhere and success is a shared effort. You also love taking things from chaos to clarity. You’re a natural at understanding ambiguous, complex problems and communicating them simply to others. You also have the drive to see things through despite changes and setbacks. You’re equally comfortable discussing detail with engineers and ideas with product managers and designers. You’re great with tech (Atlassian project management tools, basic web development) and you write a mean doc.
Also, we’d love it if you had the following but it’s not a prerequisite!
•
Knowledge of product growth strategies and user acquisition in the UK
•
Experience in marketing or advertising in the UK market
•
You’ve got a tertiary education in conversion rate optimisation, literature, or localisation
•
You have copy-writing experience — you maintain a blog or, even better, you have experience in localisation for a SaaS product
•
You showcase a solid understanding of organic growth (SEO and Wordpress)
•
You have some design experience
What's in it for you?
Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard—but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connection, and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a range of benefits to support your success inside and outside work:
• Equity packages – we want our success to be yours too
• Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
• Annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more
• Flexible leave options that let you recharge or take time to give back
Check out lifeatcanva.com for more info.

Join us in preserving engineering heritage while pioneering the future of resilient water infrastructure! You will help to deliver industry-leading reservoir and dam projects across the UK and further afield, including safety upgrades, hydropower, new storage and resilience schemes.
Our graduates gain valuable experience working on a variety of projects alongside a multitude of different disciplines. Our graduates are encouraged to develop their understanding of many elements within the water industry, such as hydraulic, structural, geotechnical and environmental design through calculations, report writing and use of engineering software. About This Job
As a Senior Quantity Surveyor, you will support our project managers and clients with the development and management of projects from concept and design, through project delivery and finally on to financial close. Projects are varied in size and scale with some at the forefront of the UK's drive to decarbonise the power industry. You will be part of a multi-disciplined team ensuring the commercial aspects of the projects are appropriately managed to the highest quality and in accordance with the client, stakeholder and/or regulatory requirements. You will support our Project Managers with contract management activities, predominately using the NEC3 and NEC4 form of contract and occasionally FIDIC based construction contracts.

• Build and maintain professional relationships with both internal and external parties
• Support the project team in establishing commercial contracts and providing risk management guidance

• Supporting the Project Manager in the preparation of Early Warnings (EW), Compensation Events (CE) and Project Managers Communications (PMI)
• Responsible for cost assurance activities on a portfolio of projects ensuring applications for payment are justified and accurate
• Provide contract and risk management support including participating in Risk Reduction meetings
• Monitor and report on expenditure on contracts compared to budgets and forecasts
• Seek to minimise the cost of a project and enhance value for money whilst still achieving the required standards and quality
• Prepare and manage cashflow forecasts
• Prepare and maintain cost reporting for internal & external stakeholders
• Assist to avoid disputes with clients, suppliers and subcontractors
• Assisting in the compilation of commercial / contractual responses to the client and subcontractors

• Ensure compliance with commercial and financial governance processes

• Experience of working on high voltage substation construction projects is desirable, although not essential

This role is hybrid on site in Murton.

Full time / 40 hours per week

About the role:
Wise moves billions across borders every year. Behind every transaction is a decision: is this safe? Our ML systems make that call - at scale, in real time, across every market we operate in.
Our Risk ML team is building the next generation of financial crime detection at Wise - investing in modern architectures like deep learning, graph neural networks, and foundation models to detect increasingly sophisticated fraud and money laundering patterns. We're looking for a Staff Applied ML Engineer to lead this evolution: defining the architecture strategy, shipping production neural models, and building the blueprint that scales across FinCrime domains.
This is a greenfield opportunity - you'll be setting the direction for how Wise applies modern ML to financial crime risk, with strong investment and engagement from senior leadership.
How we work:
Risk ML sits within Wise's FinCrime organisation, owning the full ML and AI foundation for financial crime detection. We're scaling into three dedicated pillars - Feature Platform, Learning Loop and Risk Modelling. You'll sit in Risk Modelling, working alongside data scientists, platform engineers, product and domain experts.
We operate with high autonomy and low hierarchy. You'll own problems end-to-end - from research and architecture decisions through to production deployment and impact measurement. We value engineers who shape direction, not just execute tickets.
What will you be working on?
• Designing and shipping ML and deep learning models for financial crime detection - sequence-based, graph-based, attention-based - serving real-time decisions at Wise's scale
• Defining the architecture strategy for how Wise applies modern ML to risk - which model families, which serving patterns, which training paradigms
• Building the reusable end-to-end pipeline pattern - from experimentation through training to production deployment - that future models follow
• Evaluating and prototyping foundation model and embedding approaches for transaction representation across FinCrime domains
• Partnering with Data Science on model evaluation, experimentation design and causal measurement in domains where clean A/B testing isn't always possible
• Mentoring engineers and data scientists on modern ML fundamentals, production best practices, and architectural decision-making

• Ability to make architecture-level decisions independently - model selection, training infrastructure, serving strategy - and explain the reasoning and tradeoffs
• Experience designing ML systems with hard latency and throughput requirements, including optimisation decisions (quantization, pre-computed embeddings, batching strategies)
• Strong fundamentals in deep learning: gradient dynamics, attention mechanisms, graph message-passing, sequence modelling
• Track record of influencing technical strategy across teams - you don't just build, you shape direction
• Python, PyTorch (or equivalent), distributed training, ML pipeline orchestration
Nice to Have:
• Experience in FinCrime, fraud detection, AML, or regulated financial services
• Experience with graph-based methods (GNNs, entity resolution, link analysis) in production

• Experience establishing modern ML practices in organisations scaling their ML capabilities

About This Job
Our functional specialists write reports which help the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) make important decisions about a person’s health and care.
Maybe you’re a nurse right now and you’d like to move away from direct care - this role offers you the chance to not only improve your assessment skills, but also to use your knowledge and experience to make important clinical recommendations. Or you might be an occupational therapist, physiotherapist or paramedic wanting to learn how to evaluate situations in a different way in a different setting. We’re looking for people with the compassion and experience to understand our claimants’ health conditions/disabilities and how they impact their lives.
This role is different from other healthcare professions, and that’s why we take your training and development seriously. You’ll receive comprehensive training with time set aside for self-development learning.
If you’re looking for a change, including more regular working hours, a competitive salary and are ready to expand your skills and experience, this could be the role for you.
What you’ll do in this role:
• Conduct initial reviews, face-to-face, video or telephone assessments to evaluate how a claimant’s health condition or disability affects them for various types of benefit including WCA and PIP.
• Analyse and interpret clinical information and supporting evidence.
• Write detailed evidence-based reports to support the DWP in making informed and objective decisions - no treatment or diagnosis required.
• Use IT systems to support clinical decision-making and report writing.
• Develop your clinical knowledge and constantly learn about health conditions which are less familiar to you.
What are PIP and WCA?
• Personal Independence Payment (PIP) is a benefit for people with a long-term health condition or impairment. It is paid to make a contribution to the extra costs that disabled people may face, to help them lead full, active and independent lives.
• Work Capability Assessment (WCA) is a functional assessment that looks at a range of different activities relating to physical, mental, intellectual and cognitive functions, to help DWP determine a customer's capability for work or work-related activity.

Qualifications
What we’re looking for:
• Welsh language skills (spoken and/or written) are desirable to support service users effectively
• One year's post-registration experience as a nurse (RMN, RNLD, RGN), occupational therapist, physiotherapist or paramedic
• fully registered with a relevant UK regulatory body (NMC, HCPC or other), without restriction or conditions and with a valid PIN
• excellent observational and communication skills, giving you the ability to listen, empathise and dig deeper
• the ability to work quickly, producing reports in a timely manner and hitting targets
• solid experience with using IT and Microsoft Office, as well as remotely accessing systems
• a current valid driving licence or access to a form of transport to attend your nearest assessment centre
Please note: all candidates must hold the right to work in the UK as we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.
Successful candidates will be required to successfully complete government baseline personnel security standard vetting. This is the recognised standard for the pre-employment screening of individuals with access to government asset.
This role is defined as regulated activity relating to children or vulnerable adults within the meaning of the Safeguarding Vulnerable Groups Act 2006 it is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974. At vetting, you will undergo an enhanced criminality check which will show both spent and unspent convictions.

Additional Information
Your working hours:
You’ll be contracted to work 7.5 hours per day, 37.5 hours per week (full time).  Part time options are also available - 3 days (22.5 hours) or 4 days (30 hours) per week.  Please note part-time staff will be required to work either a Monday or a Friday each week.
Please note for part-time roles the initial training period of 8 weeks (paid) is full time, so candidates must be able to commit to that.
Monday to Friday between 8am to 5pm with no weekend or night shifts (occasional 8pm finishes may be required).

We were awarded two contracts to deliver the Health Assessment Advisory Service (HAAS) assessments in the Midlands and Wales for the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), and in Northern Ireland for the Department for Communities (DfC).
We deliver assessments for a variety of different benefits, including delivering PIP assessments in the Midlands and Wales since 2013, and in Northern Ireland since 2016.

About This Job
As Enterprise Architect, you will help enable Bicycle Therapeutics’ success by shaping and delivering the technology backbone that supports our growth, pipeline and operations across Development, Supply and G&A. You will connect existing and future systems, platforms and data capabilities so teams can work effectively, make better decisions and scale with confidence, including in regulated settings where compliance, quality and data integrity matter.
This is a strategic design and delivery-focused role. You will make practical, secure and scalable technology choices, reusing and evolving existing solutions where they fit and replacing them where business needs have moved on. You will also be accountable for turning architecture direction into delivered capability, strengthening trusted data flow, data warehouse or lakehouse capabilities, analytics and AI-ready data products so data directly enables business processes, operational visibility and decision-making.
In this key technology leadership role for IT at Bicycle, reporting to the VP, IT & Cybersecurity, you will lead the technical architecture team across cloud/solution architecture, AI Ops and network/infrastructure engineering, partnering widely across Bicycle to turn architecture strategy into delivered solutions.
As a fluent communicator you will also be able to explain complex technical choices simply so leaders and teams can make confident decisions and deliver meaningful change.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
• Enterprise architecture strategy and delivery: Define, evolve and deliver the enterprise architecture roadmap across applications, data, cloud, infrastructure, integration and security, ensuring current and future systems connect effectively and support business growth.
• Connected systems and platforms: Design and deliver how existing and future platforms integrate across Development, Manufacturing and G&A, reducing fragmentation and enabling secure, scalable and reusable technology patterns.
• Data warehouse or lakehouse capabilities: Shape the architecture for trusted data flow, integration, modelling and enterprise data warehouse or lakehouse capabilities that support Development, Manufacturing and G&A business processes, reporting, insight and decision-making.

Job Title
Senior Optical Research Scientist/Engineer
Location(s)
High Wycombe
Job Description
Purpose
We are looking for an experienced optical scientist or engineer to lead the development, design and optimisation of advanced IR, UV and visible spectrometer systems. This role combines theoretical expertise with practical implementation in both research and commercial applications.
The successful candidate will develop a good understanding of the function and use of our products and their underlying technology, and will define and document both high-level functional and performance requirements and detailed sub-system requirements.
You will collaborate with key stakeholders to contribute to system design and specification, which may include concept development, design calculations or system modelling. The role includes collaboration with, and support of, PerkinElmer’s global R&D and manufacturing centres, which may involve travel.
The role also includes investigation of selected manufacturing and field failures on both new and existing products to determine root cause and initiate remedial actions.
You will have the opportunity to shape the optical design of next-generation spectroscopy instruments, working in a multidisciplinary team that covers everything from early research and new product development to sustaining existing products.
International and national travel may be required for conferences and trade shows, and to support PerkinElmer’s global R&D and manufacturing centres.
Responsibilities
Optical design and development
• Research, develop and implement optical system designs using principles of physical optics, radiometry and spectroscopy
• Drive the conceptual design and development of IR, UV and visible spectroscopic instruments
• Perform detailed optical modelling and analysis using advanced software tools (e.g. Zemax)
• Optimise and tolerance optical designs for performance and manufacturability
• Research and develop new spectroscopic techniques
• Understand and specify the products’ optical performance parameters at both system and sub-system level
Test, validation and data analysis
• Lead the validation and calibration of spectroscopic instruments
• Analyse experimental data and produce summary reports
• Work with other engineers to design and build the test equipment needed
Sustaining, product support and root cause analysis
• Lead troubleshooting and root cause analysis for both new and existing products, covering development, manufacturing and field issues, working with design engineers, manufacturing and service to understand failure modes and quality issues
Collaboration and ways of working
• Collaborate with mechanical, electrical and systems engineers on integrated product design
• Author technical documentation, reports and research papers
• Work within our structured product development process
• Take responsibility for product quality and performance
Basic Qualification
Required:
• Degree (BSc or higher) in physics or an engineering discipline
• 5+ years’ experience in optical systems development
• Proven ability to design free-space coupled relay and imaging optical systems
• Well versed in the use of Zemax (or similar software) for ray tracing, analysis and optimisation
• Experience in the specification of optical components and knowledge of their manufacturing processes.
• Experience of planning and delivering work within a structured product development process
• Proven ability to assess technical risk and recognise failure modes
• Proven ability to design and carry out experiments, and to analyse and report on the results
• Proficiency in automated data collection and analysis using suitable software
Preferred Characteristics
• Postgraduate qualification (MSc or PhD) in an engineering or physical science discipline
• Experience designing reflective optical imaging or illumination systems
• Experience in the application of diffraction gratings for spectroscopy
• Knowledge of scanning Michelson interferometers
• Experience in the design, troubleshooting and manufacture of electro-mechanical equipment (preferably instrumentation)
• Product development experience within a company making measurement instrumentation
• Familiarity with product design methodologies such as design for manufacture (DFM) and design FMEATask- and goal-oriented, with the drive to see work through to completion
• Analytical thinker, driven by data
• Strong organisational skills
• Practical problem solver, comfortable switching between long-term development and urgent manufacturing issues

saabgroup.wd116.myworkdayjobs.com/saab_c.description_excerpt:
Introduction
Saab UK is part of Scandinavia’s largest defence company, bringing together the best of Swedish and British innovation. Saab offers world-leading solutions and services in defence, aviation, space, and civil security to keep people and society safe. Our UK presence has been growing at pace, meaning we can offer a wide range of opportunities for personal fulfilment and career growth. We currently employ over 600 people across eight sites in the UK, and our specialisations include software engineering, underwater robotics, radars, AI, and armed forces training.
What you will be part of
Saab is a leading defence and security company with an enduring purpose, to help nations keep their people and society safe.
Empowered by its 28,000 talented people, Saab constantly pushes the boundaries of technology to create a safer and more sustainable world.
Saab designs, manufactures and maintains advanced systems in aeronautics, weapons, command and control, sensors and underwater systems.
Saab is headquartered in Sweden. It has major operations all over the world and is part of the domestic defence capability of several nations.
The Role:
This role is part of our Sensor Systems Radar Business in Fareham.
At Saab, we are constantly looking ahead and pushing boundaries on what´s considered technically possible. Saab is expanding in the UK and we are now seeking talented and highly motivated engineers to support our radar and sensors growth activities at our Fareham offices.
We are recruiting for a Senior Systems Engineer specialising in Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) and Distributed Sensing.
The successful candidate is expected to fulfil the requirements of a Saab Specialist, and act as a technical leader to: drive development, lead innovation and anticipate future trends, identify opportunities, mitigate risks, and advocate change to maintain competitiveness.  Also lead competence development, and formulate and maintain Specialist Work Programmes.
Key Responsibilities:
As a Senior System Engineer, you will be responsible for enhancing our current products, developing improvements and investigating new areas for product growth, as well as supporting the Engineering Team with various Systems Engineering-focussed activities.
•
System Architecture & Design.  Lead the architectural design of PNT solutions, integrating Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), Inertial Navigation Systems, and alternative PNT (e.g., vision-based, RF-based, or celestial navigation).  Architect distributed sensing networks, defining how data is collected, synchronized, and fused across multiple remote nodes to create a unified operational picture. Define system-level requirements, interface control documents, and performance specifications for timing accuracy and positioning precision.  Perform trade studies to optimise the balance between size, weight, power, and cost and system performance.
•
PNT & Synchronization Expertise.  Implement and optimise high-precision timing distribution protocols (e.g., PTP/IEEE 1588, NTP, or White Rabbit).  Develop strategies for PNT resilience, including mitigation of jamming, spoofing, and GNSS-denied environment operations.  Lead the selection and integration of atomic clocks, quantum oscillators, and high-grade IMUs.
•
Distributed Sensing & Data Fusion.  Design algorithms and architectures for distributed beamforming, phased arrays, or coordinated sensor fusion.  Manage the challenges of network latency, jitter and asynchronous data arrival in distributed sensing environments.  Collaborate with software teams to implement edge-processing capabilities to reduce data backhaul from sensing nodes.
•
Integration, Test & Evaluation.  Develop comprehensive verification and validation (V&V) plans to prove timing and positioning accuracy.  Design and execute complex test campaigns using hardware-in-the-loop and software-in-the-loop simulations.  Lead the analysis of telemetry and test data to identify systemic errors and drive corrective design changes.
•
Leadership & Mentorship.  Serve as the Subject Matter Expert for PNT and Distributed Sensing across cross-functional teams (Radio Frequency, Software, Mechanical).  Mentor junior engineers in systems engineering best practices and specialized domain knowledge.  Present technical roadmaps and progress reports to senior leadership and external.
Skills and Experience:
Required
•
Master’s or PhD in a related field.
•
A minimum of five to ten years industrial radar, communications or electronic warfare systems experience.
•
A minimum of seven years of experience in systems engineering, specifically focusing on PNT and/or distributed sensor systems.
•
Proven track record with systems utilising GNSS (GPS, Galileo, GLONASS) and Inertial Navigation (Kalman Filtering, sensor fusion).
•
Experience with distributed aperture systems, sensor networks, or Multiple-Input Multiple-Output radar architectures.
•
Proficiency with MATLAB/ Simulink for modelling and simulation.
•
Experience with Model-Based Systems Engineering tools and requirements management tools.
•
Familiar with the principles of ISO 15288:2023.
•
During your employment you will handle tasks and materials that are classified as military secret and therefore you must have a UK or Swedish citizenship.
Desirable
•
RF Knowledge: Strong understanding of RF front-end design, antenna theory and signal propagation.
•
Programming.  Proficiency in C++, Python, or Rust for prototyping algorithms.
•
Security.  Experience with encrypted PNT signals or secure timing distribution.
By submitting an application to Saab UK you consent to undertaking workforce screening activities that may include but are not limited to: Baseline Personnel Security checks, National Security Vetting, reference checks, verification of working rights and in all circumstances preferred candidates will be placed through a security interview.

About this role
Role purpose
BlackRock is seeking a Director of Technology Regulatory Compliance to develop and operate a global compliance programme addressing the rapidly evolving regulation of technology, artificial intelligence, data, cyber security, digital operational resilience and technology service providers.
The role will cover BlackRock’s distinct but interconnected responsibilities as:
• A regulated financial institution that develops and uses technology, including AI, data and cloud-based capabilities;
• A customer of third-party technology and ICT services, including cloud, managed service, software, data and AI providers; and
• A provider of technology and data services to clients, including through Aladdin, eFront and Preqin.
This dual client-and-provider perimeter creates regulatory obligations that extend beyond a traditional financial-services compliance model. The successful candidate will therefore combine technology expertise, regulatory interpretation and programme-building capability. They will work alongside the responsibilities of key BlackRock divisions such as the Aladdin business, Legal, Information Security, Risk Management and Technology & Operations.
This role will translate complex and sometimes overlapping global requirements into a coherent, risk-based Technology Compliance Programme. This will include governance, regulatory inventory and applicability, control frameworks, product compliance, assurance, regulatory engagement, management information and evidence of compliance. As such, this role requires a technology regulatory specialist who can operate credibly with engineers, technology product owners and cyber professionals as well as collaborating with key stakeholders whilst providing effective challenge and assurance from a Compliance perspective.
Key responsibilities
•
• Lead compliance oversight for BlackRock's technology businesses (Aladdin, eFront and Preqin), supporting the development of new technology products and capabilities by assessing them against relevant regulatory requirements and liaising with specialist compliance teams where financial regulatory considerations arise.
• Assess the regulatory implications of providing technology or data services to clients and identify the obligations that may attach directly to BlackRock as a  technology or data (including AI-service) provider.
• Design and implement a global, risk-based Technology Compliance Programme covering technology, AI, Cloud, data, cyber security, and operational & digital resilience requirements,  aligning to associated technology-driven regulation (e.g. DORA, EU AI Act, NIS2, US NIST, Australia Cyber Security Act).
• Establish the programme’s mandate, scope, governance, risk taxonomy, standards, procedures, control objectives and reporting arrangements.
• Maintain a global inventory of current and emerging technology-related laws, regulations, standards and supervisory expectations. Translate legal and regulatory requirements into clear business, product, technology and control requirements whilst balancing obligations with market practice.
• Define Compliance’s role relative to the, Legal, Technology Risk Management, Information Security, and other control functions, ensuring clear accountability and avoidance of control duplication.
• Continuously review and develop the compliance program based on changes to regulatory risk, business strategy, product development and supervisory priorities whilst also taking into consideration  changes to relevant laws and regulations. This includes ensuring that changes to IT services and infrastructure are evaluated, authorised, and managed in accordance with regulatory standards.,
• Develop a structured approach to identifying and managing obligations arising from BlackRock’s different roles as a financial institution ,technology provider, and AI provider/deployer
• Support the development and maintenance of IT compliance policies, technical standards, and secure configuration baselines. Ensure these are embedded into solution design, procurement, and operational processes, and are enforced through effective automation and monitoring capabilities
• Support engagements with financial, technology, AI, and cyber-security regulators globally.
•
• Represent Compliance in interactions with financial, technology, AI and cyber-security regulators globally, leading responses to regulatory enquiries, examinations, thematic reviews and supervisory engagements, and providing credible challenge and advocacy on BlackRock’s approach to technology, AI and digital resilience regulation.
Leadership and stakeholder management
• Act as a senior technology-regulatory subject-matter expert within Global Compliance.
• Build trusted relationships with senior leaders across Technology, Product, Information Security, Data, AI, Legal, Risk, Operations and Internal Audit.
• Influence technical and commercial decisions while maintaining appropriate Compliance independence.
• Build and lead a specialist team as the programme develops.
• Develop technology and digital-regulation capability across the broader Compliance function.
• Represent Compliance in relevant architecture, product, AI, data, cyber, resilience and third-party governance bodies.

As Harm Reduction Lead within Recovery Steps Cumbria, you’ll take the lead in developing and delivering a strategic harm reduction plan across the county. You’ll lead on key areas of work, including Naloxone provision, needle and syringe programmes (NSP), blood-borne virus (BBV) testing and treatment, hepatitis C provision and the prevention of drug-related deaths.
Using local, regional and national data, you’ll identify emerging trends, inform service development and help shape effective responses to the changing needs of the people we support.
You’ll also play an important role in developing peer-led approaches, including Peer-to-Peer Naloxone provision, and sharing knowledge and best practice across our services and wider professional networks.
Based at Stocklund House in Carlisle, this is a county-wide role working across six hubs and within the community. You’ll need a full driving licence and the flexibility to travel across Cumbria to work with colleagues, partner organisations and the people who use our services.

• Build effective partnerships: Work collaboratively with colleagues, partner agencies, commissioners and other stakeholders to strengthen relationships and improve outcomes across Cumbria.
• Share expertise and best practice: Attend relevant strategic meetings, forums and networks, keeping up to date with developments in harm reduction, policy and legislation.
• Promote safety and safeguarding: Identify and respond to potential risks, following organisational safeguarding procedures and working with relevant authorities where necessary.

• Experience delivering one-to-one and group interventions, alongside harm reduction training for staff and people using services.

• Experience working with carers and families.
• Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office and Outlook, alongside experience using management information systems and social media networks.
• Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work effectively with a wide range of colleagues, partners and stakeholders.

• Information Technology
• Software engineering

Security Clearance
Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.  Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.

• Time to recharge: Enjoy generous leave with the opportunity to accrue up to 12 additional flexi-days each year.

• Your wellbeing matters: Free access to mental health support, financial advice, and employee-led networks championing inclusion and diversity (Enable, Pride, Equalise, Armed Forces, Carers, Wellbeing and Ethnicity).

Location: Stansted, United Kingdom

Our Team:
Semtech’s High-Speed IC Design team is a highly experienced and collaborative engineering group developing industry-leading analog and mixed-signal solutions for next-generation optical communication systems.
The team operates across Stansted (UK) and Ottawa (Canada), working closely with global colleagues to deliver high-performance transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs) and laser driver ICs supporting data rates up to 200G. These technologies are critical to enabling the continued growth of data centres, 5G infrastructure, and fibre-to-the-home networks.
Job Summary:
The Analog Design Manager leads analog and mixed-signal design engineering activities across multiple high-speed IC product lines, owning the full new product introduction (NPI) lifecycle from product definition through to volume production.
The role is responsible for directing a multidisciplinary team of circuit designers and layout engineers, driving technical execution across concurrent development programmes, and ensuring robust delivery of high-performance IC designs aligned to business and customer requirements.
Responsibilities:
• Lead and manage a multidisciplinary team of analog circuit designers and layout engineers, including goal setting, performance management, recruitment, and capability development (20%).
• Own end-to-end NPI execution across multiple high-speed IC programmes, from concept and architecture through to tape-out, qualification, and production ramp (25%).
• Translate product roadmap and system requirements into executable analog design plans, ensuring alignment with schedule, cost, and performance targets (10%).
• Drive design execution across concurrent programmes, including scheduling, resource planning, and risk management (10%).
• Collaborate closely with Marketing, Product Definition, Applications, Product Engineering, Test, Validation, and Reliability teams to ensure full alignment with customer and system requirements (10%).
• Lead pre-tape-out reviews, ensuring design compliance against specification, layout verification, and production readiness (10%).
• Oversee post-silicon bring-up, silicon correlation, and performance optimisation to improve first-pass success rates and product maturity (10%).
• Prepare and present technical updates, design reviews, and programme status reporting to senior leadership, ensuring clear visibility of risks, milestones, and delivery progress (5%).
Minimum Qualifications:
• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical or Electronic Engineering, or related technical discipline required
• 10+ years’ experience in semiconductor analog design required
• 5+ years’ experience in a leadership or engineering management role required
• Hands-on experience in analog circuit design, mixed-signal integration, simulation, and IC verification
• Proven experience leading NPI programmes within semiconductor development environments
• Strong ability to manage multiple concurrent projects under schedule and resource constraints
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills across cross-functional engineering organisations
Desired Qualifications:
• Master’s degree in Electrical or Electronic Engineering or related discipline preferred
• Experience in optical communication IC design, including laser drivers and transimpedance amplifiers
• Experience with SAP, semiconductor design tools, and advanced analog simulation environments
• Experience supporting or leading high-speed IC development programmes through full product lifecycle
• Exposure to semiconductor device physics and analog design optimisation techniques
• Experience implementing engineering standards, methodologies, or design governance frameworks
• • Project or programme management certification (e.g., PMP) preferred

This role is an outstanding platform to grow as both an engineering leader and a technical authority, with a clear pathway into more senior leadership as the business continues to scale.

Location: London – Multi-Site
Competitive Salary + Benefits
Lead safety across one of London’s largest bus operations

Lead and develop the health and safety strategy across our London operations

Provide expert advice and guidance to senior leaders and operational teams

Drive a proactive, positive and accountable safety culture across the business
•
Maintain a strong and visible presence across our London garages and operational locations
•
Monitor safety performance, identify trends and ensure appropriate actions are taken

Lead continuous improvement initiatives to reduce risk and improve safety performance

Ensure compliance with relevant health and safety legislation, regulatory requirements and Arriva standards
•
Oversee investigations into significant incidents and ensure lessons learned are embedded across the business
•
Provide constructive challenge and assurance to operational and engineering leaders
•
Develop and maintain effective risk management, audit and assurance processes
•
Engage colleagues at all levels, ensuring safety is understood as everyone's responsibility
•
Work collaboratively with wider Arriva teams and key external stakeholders

Significant experience leading health and safety within a large, complex and operationally focused organisation

Experience within transport, logistics, engineering, fleet, manufacturing or another safety-critical environment

Strong knowledge of UK health and safety legislation and best practice

Experience of developing and implementing health and safety strategy

Strong investigation, risk management, audit and assurance experience

The confidence to challenge constructively and influence senior stakeholders

Excellent communication and leadership skills

The ability and willingness to travel regularly across Arriva London's sites

accenture.wd103.myworkdayjobs.com/accent.description_excerpt:
Oracle OCI Multi-Cloud Engineer / Associate Manager
Location: London, hybrid
Role Overview
We are seeking an experienced OCI & Multi-Cloud Engineer / Solution Architect with deep expertise in Oracle technologies and hyperscaler cloud platforms. This is a senior technical role responsible for designing, delivering, and operating Oracle-centric cloud architectures across OCI, Azure, AWS, and GCP. The successful candidate will combine strong Oracle database and EBS administration skills with cloud and solution architecture expertise, playing a key role in data centre exit programmes, cloud migrations, and the design of secure, scalable landing zones. The role requires the ability to operate as a trusted technical advisor — translating complex business requirements into robust, deliverable solution designs.
Key Responsibilities
Solution Architecture
• Act as Solution Architect across Oracle and multi-cloud programmes, owning the end-to-end technical solution from initial requirements through to delivery and handover
• Engage with business and technical stakeholders to elicit, shape, and translate requirements into viable, cost-effective solution designs
• Produce and present solution proposals, architecture options papers, and business cases to senior stakeholders and governance boards
• Lead architecture assurance and design authority reviews, ensuring solutions meet security, performance, resilience, and compliance requirements
• Define solution patterns and reference architectures for Oracle cloud workloads that can be reused across programmes
• Manage technical risk throughout the solution lifecycle, identifying issues early and proposing mitigations
• Work closely with programme and project managers to ensure solution integrity is maintained through delivery
• Support pre-sales and bid activity by contributing to RFP/RFI responses, statements of work, and effort estimation
Cloud Architecture & Design
• Design and deliver High-Level Designs (HLD) and Low-Level Designs (LLD) for Oracle and multi-cloud infrastructure solutions
• Architect and build Cloud Landing Zones across OCI and hyperscaler platforms (Azure, AWS, GCP), including network topology, identity, governance, and security guardrails
• Define and implement multi-cloud integration patterns including hybrid connectivity, cross-cloud networking, and unified identity management
• Produce architecture documentation, solution blueprints, and technical runbooks
• Lead technical design workshops and engage with stakeholders at all levels
Oracle Database Administration
• Administer and optimise Oracle Database environments (11g, 12c, 19c and above) on-premises and in cloud
• Manage Oracle Database Service deployments across OracleDB@Azure, OracleDB@AWS, and OracleDB@GCP
• Perform database performance tuning, patching, backup and recovery, and capacity planning
• Manage Oracle RAC, Data Guard, and ASM environments
• Support Oracle Advanced Security features including TDE, audit vault, and database firewall
Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS)
• Administer and support Oracle EBS environments (R12.1, R12.2) including patching, cloning, and upgrades
• Perform EBS cloning (full and rapid clone) for development, test, and DR environments
• Lead and deliver EBS migrations to cloud (OCI, Azure, AWS), including lift-and-shift and re-platform approaches
• Configure and manage EBS shared application tier, concurrent managers, and autoconfig
• Manage EBS integrations, middleware, and WebLogic/OHS components
• Work with functional teams to support EBS application patching and critical patch updates (CPUs)
Data Centre Exit & Cloud Migration
• Lead data centre exit programmes, including asset discovery, dependency mapping, wave planning, and cut-over execution
• Deliver database migration projects using Oracle Data Pump, GoldenGate, RMAN, and cloud-native migration services (DMS, OCI DMS)
• Execute lift-and-shift, re-platform, and re-architecture migration strategies based on business requirements
• Manage migration runbooks, rollback plans, and post-migration validation
• Assess on-premises workloads for cloud readiness and produce TCO/ROI analysis
Linux & Infrastructure
• Administer Linux environments (RHEL, Oracle Linux, CentOS) including kernel tuning, storage configuration, and performance optimisation for Oracle workloads
• Manage storage configurations for Oracle (ASM, NFS, block storage) in cloud and on-premises environments
• Script and automate infrastructure tasks using Shell, Python, Ansible, or Terraform
• Configure and manage Oracle Hugepages, NUMA, and OS-level tuning for database performance

Contractor Supervising Officer (CSO)
Location: Filton, Bristol
Hours: Monday to Friday, 07:00 – 15:30
Contract Type: Permanent
About the Role
We are seeking an experienced and highly organised Contractor Supervising Officer to join our waste management team at our Filton, Bristol site. This is a critical supervisory role overseeing the safe collection and disposal of hazardous and non-hazardous waste via tanker and skip operations, ensuring full compliance with health, safety, and environmental regulations.
As the CSO, you will function as the primary point of contact for waste contractors, managing all aspects of tanker and skip operations including scheduling, site access, road closures, and ensuring strict adherence to waste handling procedures. Your expertise will be essential in maintaining operational safety and regulatory compliance across all waste removal activities
What your day to day will look like
Contractor Supervision and Management To supervise waste contractors during tanker and skip operations for both hazardous and non-hazardous waste collection. This includes conducting safety briefings, monitoring contractor activities, ensuring compliance with site rules and permit-to-work systems, and acting as the authoritative site representative throughout all waste uplift operations.
Road Closure Coordination To plan, arrange and manage temporary road closures required for safe tanker and skip collection vehicle access and positioning. Coordinating with site operations, communicating with affected departments, implementing appropriate traffic management measures and ensuring minimal disruption to site activities whilst maintaining safety standards.
Waste Verification and Compliance Before any waste leaves site you will verify that all materials are correctly identified, classified and labelled in accordance with regulatory requirements and waste transfer documentation. Inspect waste collected from buildings and loaded into skips ensuring proper segregation and labelling preventing non-compliant materials from entering the waste stream.
Health and Safety Leadership You will conduct risk assessments for tanker and skip operations, implement control measures, and ensure all activities are conducted safely. This includes monitoring for potential hazards, enforcing the use of appropriate PPE, and stopping work immediately if unsafe conditions are identified.
Building Collection Oversight, you will oversee the collection of waste from various buildings across the site, ensuring waste operatives follow correct procedures for handling, labelling, and transporting materials. You will inspect collection points to verify compliance with waste segregation requirements.
Communication and Coordination Acting as the liaison between contractors, site management, waste operatives, and other stakeholders, you will ensure clear communication of schedules, requirements, and any operational changes. You will escalate issues promptly and work collaboratively to resolve problems efficiently.
Emergency Response In the event of spills, leaks, or other incidents during waste operations, you will coordinate the immediate response, ensure appropriate containment measures are implemented, and manage reporting procedures in accordance with site protocols.
Essential Requirements
Proven experience in waste management operations, particularly supervising contractor activities including tanker and skip operations involving hazardous materials. Knowledge of hazardous waste regulations, classification systems (EWC codes), and waste transfer documentation is essential. Experience in an industrial, manufacturing, or large-scale facilities environment is highly desirable.
Technical Knowledge Strong understanding of health and safety requirements for hazardous waste handling, including COSHH assessments, permit-to-work systems, and emergency response procedures. Familiarity with environmental legislation and duty of care obligations for waste producers is required.
Leadership and Communication Skills Excellent supervisory capabilities with the confidence to challenge unsafe practices and enforce compliance. Strong communication skills, both verbal and written, with the ability to consult effectively with contractors, management, and operational teams. Experience managing multiple tasks simultaneously and making decisions under pressure.
Organisational Abilities Exceptional diligence with the ability to plan and coordinate complex operations involving multiple stakeholders. Strong administrative skills for maintaining accurate records and documentation. Ability to anticipate potential issues and implement initiative-taking solutions.
Licenses and Certifications Relevant health and safety qualifications such as IOSH Managing Safely or equivalent are desirable. Any specific waste management qualifications (e.g., WAMITAB) would be advantageous. Computer literacy for documentation and reporting purposes is required.
Personal Attributes You must be assertive, confident, and able to maintain authority when supervising contractors and enforcing safety standards. A methodical approach, strong problem-solving abilities, and the resilience to work in challenging outdoor conditions are essential. Reliability and punctuality are critical.
Availability You must be available to work the fixed shift pattern of 07:00 to 15:30, Monday to Friday,
with the flexibility to adapt to operational demands when necessary.

Join us in taking the more inspiring, innovative, and optimistic path on our journey toward success as a Contractor Supervising Officer in Filton Bristol.

We believe in better. And we make it happen.
Better content. Better products. And better careers.

And we do it all right here at Sky.
The Core responsibility of the Playout Controller is to manage the transmission of ‘Live’ complex events, as well as to provide schedule management, output monitoring and first line recovery for any Sky hosted channels.
The management of ‘live’ complex events includes, for example: broadcasts where the break structure is variable, the duration of the event is unpredictable or where the timings of two subsequent events may overlap.
Schedule management includes the preparation, checking and updating of automation schedules delivered into the area to ensure discrepancies are identified before the output is affected. It also includes the alteration of “live” automation schedules due to changing editorial or commercial requirements. For both the preparation and management of the automation schedules, a high degree of attention to detail and adherence to agreed process is necessary to avoid potential impact to the channel output.
Through monitoring of the channel outputs the Controller is responsible for the scheduled content being delivered to the distribution platforms without defect or degradation. Direct “eyeball” monitoring of the channel output is supported and enhanced through the use of automated fault detection and alarming which the Controller must be fully capable of interpreting and interrogating.
In the case of any fault or deviation from the required output it is the Controller’s responsibility to minimise impact to the viewing public either through restoration of service or by fault management. Knowledge of the playout infrastructure and agreed best practices for recovery are essential in performing this function effectively.
The Controller is skilled in the management of both server-based content and “live” content including complex live events.
The Controller will also be responsible for effective training of others, contributing to the integration of new systems and services. The Controller will prioritise incidents and escalate effectively, taking financial, reputational and stakeholder concerns into account.
What you’ll do
•
Schedule Preparation - performing required manual and automated tasks on the playout schedules to identify potential errors and known faults and ensure readiness for broadcast
•
Live schedule management – editing of live automation schedule to alter content or timings as required
•
Live schedule monitoring – monitoring the output of channels to confirm and maintain fault-free playout
•
Regulatory Knowledge – knowledge of Ofcom regulations and Sky policies
•
Fault Identification – immediate identification of any loss or degradation of the channel outputs, as well as loss of encryption or PIN protection
•
Fault recovery – use of system resilience or schedule editing to recover from channel loss or degradation
•
Fault management – use of on-screen messages, voice-overs, or other messaging to keep customers informed when a fault is not immediately recoverable
•
Escalation – efficient communication to 2nd line support teams and operational management
•
Editorial Knowledge – knowledge of Sky’s programming and promotional strategies.
•
Logging & Reporting – accurately recording any faults, changes, or other deviations from the originally scheduled content
•
Information Management – accurately passing on information to colleagues or operational management to ensure channel continuity
•
Communication – concise and accurate verbal and written communication, professional and courteous at all times
•
Training – passing on knowledge and experience of workflows, systems and procedures as required. Structured training of others utilising established training materials as required
•
Support – Provides support to the Playout Specialist and Operational Lead functions as required
•
Complex Live Event Management – line-up, preparation and control of complex live events including negotiation with production teams when event durations are variable or overlapping
•
Gallery Free Production – making any necessary editorial decisions to maintain channel continuity when communication with event source is incoming only e.g. World Feed
What you’ll bring
•
Qualifications - degree qualification or relevant vocational qualifications
•
Specialist Knowledge – skilled in Playout systems and workflows, skilled in managing live events, skilled in Playout systems used by Sky, skilled in managing live Sports events
•
Industry Experience – Experience of digital playout environment, complex Live broadcast experience
•
Leadership Skills - Excellent communication & influencing skills, excellent decision making and prioritisation skills
The Sky Playout Team works 24/7 365 days a year to ensure that Sky Customers are receiving the best quality live sports and entertainment programmes. You’ll be joining the team and working a fixed shift pattern of day, mid and night shifts.

Sky Q, for the TV you love all in one place
