The Head of Fire, Health & Safety is responsible for ensuring a positive safety culture is embedded across Harrods, while ensuring legislative requirements are met and safety-related risks are effectively managed.
You will lead the strategic development and delivery of our Fire, Health & Safety strategy, policies, standards and operational plans, ensuring the highest levels of compliance across our estate. This includes our iconic Knightsbridge store, production kitchens, warehouses and distribution centre.
Working closely with the Director of Security, you will provide strategic leadership and expert advice across all aspects of fire, health and safety and risk management, with the safety of our colleagues and customers at the heart of everything you do.
You will also lead and develop a multi-disciplinary, experienced team across Health & Safety and Fire, creating a high-performing, engaged team focused on continuous improvement.
About the Role
As Head of Fire, Health & Safety, you will:
• Develop and deliver the strategic vision for Fire, Health & Safety across the business and ensure it is embedded.
• Act as the organisation's subject matter expert, providing senior-level advice and guidance on fire, health and safety, building safety and risk.
• Ensure policies, procedures and operational standards remain compliant with legislation and recognised best practice.
• Provide specialist advice on building projects and upgrades, including the review of plans and proposed works.
• Oversee significant risk assessments, audits and assurance activities across the business.
• Lead the investigation and analysis of serious incidents, ensuring lessons are identified and appropriate actions implemented.
• Monitor fire safety compliance, including the adequacy and maintenance of firefighting equipment and associated controls.
• Develop effective governance, reporting, KPIs and management information, presenting key risks and findings to senior leaders and external stakeholders where required.
• Drive continuous improvement, proactively challenging the business and promoting a strong, positive safety culture.
• Lead, coach and develop your team, setting clear expectations and creating an environment of high performance, engagement and accountability.
• Deputise for the Director of Security when required, taking responsibility for strategic and operational decision-making in their absence.
About You
You will be an experienced Fire, Health & Safety leader with the credibility and expertise to operate effectively at a senior level within a complex, fast-paced organisation.
You will have:
• A NEBOSH Diploma in Occupational Health and Safety, a Health and Safety Degree, or a Level 6 NVQ.
• Chartered Membership of IOSH (CMIOSH), or be working towards this.
• Extensive knowledge of Health & Safety, Fire Safety and Building Safety legislation and the ability to translate regulatory requirements into practical solutions.
• Strong governance and assurance experience, including presenting risk and compliance information at executive level.
• A track record of developing and delivering strategic Fire, Health & Safety plans, supported by clear KPIs and measurable outcomes.
• Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to balance commercial priorities with regulatory compliance and best practice.
• Strong risk management and decision-making capability, with a proactive and pragmatic approach.
• Excellent communication and leadership skills, with the confidence to engage and challenge senior leaders, operational teams, regulators and external partners.
• Proven senior leadership experience in leading, developing and motivating Health, Safety and Fire Safety professionals, fostering a high-performing culture focused on compliance, risk reduction and continuous improvement. A demonstrable passion for Health & Safety.
Working Pattern
This is a highly visible, operational leadership role and we prefer five days per week on site, with a minimum of four days on site. The role requires flexibility to work across our sites.
The working pattern will include approximately one weekend in every six, with two days off in lieu during the week. Bank and Public Holidays are considered normal working days, and occasional additional or changed hours may be required to meet the needs of the business.
Uniquely You
At Harrods, we believe anything is possible. We celebrate and welcome applications from all cultures, backgrounds, tastes and experiences, and we're proud to create an environment where people from all walks of life can grow and thrive. What makes you unique makes us exceptional.
If you want to know more about life at Harrods, search #TogetherHarrods on LinkedIn, or follow us on Instagram @togetherharrods.

theirc.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/external_ca.description_excerpt:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
Background
The Violence Prevention and Response Unit (VPRU) is one of IRC's four Technical Units, bringing together Child Protection, Women's Protection and Empowerment, and Protection Rule of Law across over 35 countries. VPRU is increasingly strengthening connective tissue across GBV, child protection, and case management through a shared social work systems lens, in service of IRC's Safety Strategy. IRC's Technical Excellence teams offer five core services to IRC country programs: Program Design, Quality Assurance, Business Development, Research and Learning, and External Influence.
Job Overview
The WPE field is at a strategic inflection point. The humanitarian system is contracting, siloed sectoral programming by default is under scrutiny, and the organizations that will define the next decade of protection practice are those that can ground a social work systems approach in feminist practice, building connective tissue with child protection, rule of law, and case management bridge prevention and response as two expressions of a single protective logic , and take seriously the financing of services for those most at risk of violence as a structural condition of impact rather than a donor-cycle variable.
The Global Lead, Women's Protection and Empowerment Systems Transformation is hired for this moment. They are IRC's organizational leader on GBV prevention and response and women's and girls' empowerment, a core member of the VPRU senior management team, and the person responsible for transforming how IRC delivers, finances, and positions its WPE work at a critical juncture for the sector. The role carries the full authority of a senior staff member and demands intellectual independence, diagnostic acuity, and appetite for institution-building.
A deliberate attention to financing is central to the mandate: how services are resourced, how prevention and livelihoods approaches are financed as integral parts of the protection architecture, and how IRC engages donors, governments, and multilateral actors to build more durable financing models for WPE outcomes — whether or not these are delivered by humanitarian actors. IRC's WPE work spans humanitarian response, recovery, and system strengthening, and this role's financing agenda is shaped by that full arc across the humanitarian-development-peace nexus.
Major Responsibilities
Strategy, program design and business development
•
Lead the transformation of IRC's WPE practice, acting as the organizational reference point on GBV prevention and response, women's empowerment, and WPE systems strengthening, internally and externally.
•
Lead strategic direction for WPE in line with S100 and the Safety Strategy; identify global areas of programmatic risk and elevate issues to Regional Leads and VPRU leadership.
•
Lead global business development for WPE, bringing a clear distinction between financing for portfolio growth and financing for the quality, continuity, and sustainability of services. Advocate for funding architectures that cover the workforce, systems, referral infrastructure, and community relationships that make delivery possible — not only project outputs.
•
Steer the adaptation of the WPE operating model to current conditions without compromising service integrity. Revenue generation matters as a condition of sustaining the mission, not as the mission itself, and the Global Lead holds both imperatives with clear-eyed honesty.
•
Collaborate with Global Practice Leads and Regional Leads to promote programmatic synergies within WPE and across IRC sectors, with explicit attention to shared models with Child Protection and Case Management as foundational components of a social work systems approach.
•
Line manage global practice area and strategic project staff; manage in partnership other roles as applicable.
Global practice implementation support
•
Accountable for evidence-based technical oversight of WPE standards, methodologies, and tools, including cross-cutting issues such as diversity, inclusion, and climate adaptation; and for building working fluency in case management strategy and information system architecture.
•
Approach quality as a diagnostic function, not a compliance one: distinguish between failures of implementation logic, funding or capacity constraints, context shifts that have rendered approaches maladapted, and policies that have not kept pace with the communities they serve. Ask not only whether targets are being met but whether the right targets are being pursued, and act on that diagnosis in partnership with country and regional teams.
•
Support Regional Leads, Technical Advisors, and Technical Coordinators with thorny technical problems, capacity strengthening, mentorship, and career planning.
Research, data, knowledge management and learning
•
Bring intellectual credibility to debates about evidence standards: make a rigorous case for implementation learning, longitudinal qualitative evidence, cross-system data linkage, practice-based inquiry, and community-level outcome tracking as legitimate, ethical, and contextually generative forms of knowledge alongside experimental evidence. Hold both orientations without collapsing into relativism.
•
Guide research and evidence use with a genuine intelligence orientation: read across datasets — SRH, mental health, social protection, GBV — to build a coherent narrative on violence and help-seeking behavior. Be as interested in what the data cannot see as in what it shows; understand why certain populations and outcomes remain unmeasured, and treat those gaps as arguments for where the sector needs to go. Familiarity with data architectures in social welfare, public health, or financing systems adjacent to humanitarian protection is a meaningful asset.
•
Establish and maintain relevant Communities of Practice; provide technical inputs to WPE-specific MEAL tools; support data interpretation in learning routines.
External influence, representation and thought leadership
•
Exercise entrepreneurial judgment in external representation: identify where consequential conversations about women's safety, protection systems, and financing are happening before the WPE sector has found them, and…

The ERP Product Manager role exists to establish clear ownership of Apollo’s D365 F&O environment and turn it into a strategically managed business platform rather than a reactive support service. The role is accountable for ensuring the ERP environment remains stable, governed, prioritised and aligned to business objectives, while working closely with stakeholders across Apollo to identify opportunities for innovation, process improvement and operational efficiency. Over time, this role will be pivotal in shaping a scalable, well-controlled ERP platform that not only supports Apollo today, but also creates the foundation for future Apollo group companies to join the solution in a structured and sustainable way. In doing so, the role is intended to increase the value the business gets from D365, reduce inefficiency, strengthen internal ownership, and help Apollo operate more effectively as it grows.
Key Responsibilities
1. ERP Product Ownership
• Own the D365 F&O platform as a business product, ensuring clear accountability for roadmap, priorities, service performance and continuous improvement.
• Act as the primary internal owner of the ERP environment, ensuring the platform supports business operations effectively and evolves in a controlled, value-led way.
2. Governance, Demand and Prioritisation
• Own and operate the ERP governance cadence, including service reviews, change reviews, prioritisation forums and decision-making structures.
• Maintain a clear single front door for ERP business demand, ensuring requirements, issues, enhancements and optimisation ideas are triaged consistently and prioritised against business value, risk and capacity.
• Ensure ERP demand is translated into a managed, visible backlog with agreed priorities, ownership and delivery expectations.
3. Lifecycle, Releases and Environment Control
• Own the ERP release calendar and lifecycle approach, including readiness gates, go/no-go decisions, environment discipline and release governance.
• Ensure product updates, configuration changes, improvements and platform changes are planned, communicated and delivered in a controlled way.
• Work with business SMEs, internal IT and external partners to ensure release readiness, testing discipline and deployment confidence.
4. Partner and Supplier Management
• Own the operational relationship with D365 managed service, support and delivery partners.
• Manage partner performance, escalation, service reporting and commercial discipline to ensure delivery aligns with business objectives and agreed standards.
• Maintain clear boundaries between BAU support, project delivery, optimisation work and hypercare to avoid unmanaged ownership gaps.
5. Continuous Improvement and Optimisation
• Proactively identify opportunities to improve the ERP platform, simplify processes, reduce friction and increase business value.
• Work with business stakeholders to shape and prioritise optimisations, ensuring improvements are aligned to the wider business roadmap and platform standards.
• Own the ERP improvement backlog and ensure incremental change is driven purposefully rather than reactively.
6. Product Roadmap and Business Alignment
• Define and maintain the ERP roadmap, balancing operational stability, technical debt, mandatory updates, risk reduction and business-led change.
• Ensure the business understands what is planned, why it is prioritised and what value it is expected to deliver.
• Act as the bridge between business process needs and ERP platform direction.
7. Standards, Controls and Platform Guardrails
• Define and maintain ERP standards covering platform usage, integrations, controls, change discipline, documentation and configuration governance.
• Ensure appropriate controls and guardrails exist around access, change, environment use and platform decision-making.
• Protect the integrity of the ERP environment by ensuring changes are consistent with agreed standards and architecture principles.
8. Documentation and Platform Knowledge
• Ensure ERP platform documentation remains current, structured and useful, including configurations, procedures, key decisions, environment information and operating guidance.
• Strengthen internal ownership and knowledge retention so the environment is less dependent on third parties over time.
9. Stakeholder Management
• Build effective working relationships across Finance, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Warehouse, Quality, Engineering and IT stakeholders.
• Translate technical or platform constraints into sensible business decisions and communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Act as the accountable point of contact for ERP platform decisions, priorities and issues.
Scope Boundaries
In Scope
• D365 Finance & Operations platform ownership.
• ERP governance, prioritisation, roadmap, lifecycle and release management.
• Managed partner and support partner accountability.
• Continuous improvement, optimisation intake and business-driven enhancement prioritisation.
Out of Scope
• Hands-on development build work as a primary responsibility.
• Power BI platform ownership / BI delivery management.
• CRM/CE product ownership and business ownership.
Skills & Experience
Essential
• Strong experience with Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations in a live, business-critical environment.
• Proven experience in ERP service ownership, application/product ownership, ERP management, or a similar senior techno-functional platform role.
• Strong understanding of ERP governance, prioritisation, lifecycle management and controlled change.
• Strong stakeholder engagement skills and the ability to translate business demand into prioritised platform work.
• Strong partner/vendor management capability.
• Ability to bring structure, accountability and commercial focus to a business-critical ERP landscape.
Desirable
• Manufacturing, supply chain or warehouse process knowledge.
• Experience in a product-led or platform-owner style role.
• Familiarity with integrations, platform controls, testing governance and release planning.
• Microsoft D365 certifications such as MB-310, MB-500 or MB-700.
What Success Looks Like
• There is one clear accountable owner for D365 F&O.
• ERP business demand is triaged and prioritised consistently.
• The platform has a visible roadmap and release cadence.
• Third-party partners are managed tightly against expectations.
• ERP changes are more controlled, better communicated and more clearly linked to business value.
• The D365 environment is no longer seen as “just a support system”, but as a managed business product.

The Core IP Security team designs, builds and operates the bespoke security systems that protect the firm’s most sensitive intellectual property across its full lifecycle, from research through to production systems.

Nice to have:

Job Description:
Do you have Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) experience? Our market leading SPA team at Grant Thornton is hiring at all grades to continue our rapid growth! We work with corporates, private equity houses and other investors across a wide range of sectors, advising on the financial aspects of acquisitions and disposals, from completion mechanisms and price adjustments through to sale and purchase agreement (SPA) negotiations. We are seeking ADs with the technical and commercial skills who enjoy protecting value for clients undertaking acquisitions and disposals. Successful candidates should have transactions experience, a good understanding of completion mechanisms, enterprise to equity value bridges and the financial aspects of SPAs. Candidate will ideally have 3-5 years’ transaction and/or SPA advisory experience and be ACA (or equivalent) qualified.
A look into the role
As a SPA Associate Director within our team, you will:
·        Take responsibility and ownership of the client relationship at the appropriate level in the client's organisation at board level.
·        Consult effectively with specialists within the firm when faced with complex risk management.
·        Oversee and manage letters of engagement internally and with the client.
·        Develop solutions to complex technical issues.
·        Interpret and analyse complex information, identifying business issues and applying technical knowledge appropriately.
·        Oversee the preparation of deliverables to client, such as financial analysis, ensuring quality output is produced which is relevant to the transaction.
·        Lead on completion mechanism matters, including net debt, working capital and other price adjustment calculations, ensuring analysis is robust and well supported.
·        Review final drafts of our output.
·        Manage all aspects of the transaction competently, including managing any junior team members involved on the project on technical aspects of the transaction.
·        Set the fee estimate and oversees the drafting of the engagement letter.
·        Lead the presentation of conclusions and recommendations to the client and discuss the implications and action points.
·        Proactively seek out business development opportunities.
·        Suggest innovative selling solutions whilst pro-actively identifying cross-selling opportunity.
·        Review and participate in negotiations on the financial aspects of SPAs, including warranties, indemnities and disclosure letters, working closely with legal advisers.
·        Lead, motivate and coach managers by inducting effectively, giving regular feedback and timely performance reviews.
·        Prepare fee estimates and budgets for client assignments and manage client expectations about changes and overruns.
Knowing you’re right for us
Joining us as a SPA AD, the minimum criteria you’ll need is a professional qualification (ACA, ICAS, CA, ACCA or CIPFA) with post qualification transaction advisory experience (ideally 3-5 years, gained within a transaction services, corporate finance or SPA advisory environment), and to be confident managing a portfolio of SPA advisory engagements.
It would be great if you had some of the following skills, but don’t worry if you don’t tick every box, we’ll help you develop along the way:
·         Some years experience in transactions/deals including experience of advising on financial aspects of SPAs
·        Strong technical understanding of completion mechanisms, including locked box and completion accounts structures, and net debt and working capital adjustments.
·        Experience reviewing and negotiating the financial aspects of SPAs, including warranties and indemnities.
·        A level of business development experience, including converting sales opportunities and building long-term client relationships.
·        Experience managing and developing junior team members across multiple, concurrent engagements.
·        Strong report writing and communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial analysis clearly to clients and other stakeholders.
Knowing we’re right for you
The culture at Grant Thornton is what sets us apart, we’re known for our inclusive culture and creating environments where all our people can flourish. The things that set you apart, we value them, and this helps us all to perform at our best.
Our values are the unwavering principles that shape our daily behaviours and decisions, alongside our drive to do the right thing. We’re looking for people who align with our values and are purposefully driven, actively curious and candid but kind. You can learn more about our values in practice here.
It’s not just about our culture and values, in addition to a competitive salary and reward package, us you’ll also get:
Tailored development programmes and access to coaching
Flexible bank holidays – allowing you to celebrate the days that are important to you
Benefits including pension, life assurance and private medical, additional holiday purchasing and health benefits
Anytime benefits giving you access to shopping discounts, gym memberships, financial advice
And more. Visit our benefits section to read more.
How we work
We have a trust-based way of working, driven by responsible people who have the best interests of our firm and our clients at heart. Our how we work framework gives flexibility in where, how, and when we work to deliver the best results for our clients, whilst helping you keep a balance between work and life. Life is more than work, the things you do, and the people you’re with outside of work matter, that’s why we’re happy to look at flexible working options for all our roles.  That is how it should be.
We’re looking for people who can help drive the business forward, who want to contribute, spark fresh ideas and go beyond expectations. People who want to be able to proudly do what’s right, for the firm, our clients, our people and themselves. It’s how it should be.

Job Title
Conversational AI Manager
Job Description
So, who are we?
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in
established businesses.
The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.
Join us at IG – the future gets built here.
Your team:
AI Operations owns reducing the cost of serving IG’s clients, using AI, automation and channel change as its levers, while protecting the quality of the client experience.
Your role in the Team’s Success:
This role owns the performance of our live AI agent, how well it serves clients today, and how much better it serves them each week. The technology is operated by a platform partner who also builds the procedures, but everything that is live belongs to this role.
Your manager owns new capability, strategy, the API integration roadmap, and expansion into channels not yet running. You own the running system: performance, optimisation, configuration changes, simple new procedures, thresholds and escalation design. You are also the platform partner’s primary day-to-day contact, the person who holds them to their commitments and reads their reporting sceptically.
This is not a vendor management role. You are accountable for how well the agent serves clients, week by week, and for proving it.
What you'll do:
• Own live performance: resolution rate is our primary metric with repeat contact and journey CSAT tracked on every change, so removed contact is a solved problem rather than a displaced one.
• Own the ongoing optimisation roadmap: a prioritised backlog of configuration changes and new procedures, sequenced weekly and defended on evidence
• Diagnose underperformance to root cause using your own case sampling, referred and declined case analysis, complaint themes and advisor insight, rather than the partner’s reporting alone
• Build and run the experimentation practice: hypotheses, primary and guardrail metrics, sample sizes set before launch, stopping rules, and results that actually change what we do
• Ensure any implementations are/remain compliant with the relevant regulatory framework
• Own and confirm the eligibility rules and confidence thresholds applied to automated decisions, and justify to Compliance if required.
• Act as the platform partner’s primary counterpart holding them to committed delivery timelines and escalating within their organisation when work is not moving
• Take ownership of each new capability at go-live, having set the client requirements and accuracy standards for it before build started
What you’ll need:
• A track record of owning a conversational AI service, in a high-volume regulated environment, with results you can speak to precisely: the baseline, what changed, and how it was proven
• Experience managing a delivery partner you depended on for execution, where you held someone to a commitment and kept the relationship intact
• Hands-on experimentation on live client journeys: sizing samples in advance and having abandoned your own idea when the numbers did not support it
• A data-led approach: comfortable in contact analytics, measurement design and structured root-cause analysis, and hard to sell to
• Product management craft: outcome ownership, prioritisation by value, backlog discipline, in-life iteration
• Enough technical fluency to be a peer to an engineering-minded manager: you can discuss what an API can realistically return and push back on a proposed design
• Awareness of IG’s regulatory context, including Consumer Duty outcomes and the needs of vulnerable clients, in how automated decisions are designed and measured
What success looks like
By the end of year one:
• Optimisation runs as a weekly rhythm rather than a series of reactions, with a backlog that always holds the next evidenced change
• Experiments land on a regular cadence and have changed decisions, including at least one change killed because the data did not support it
• Every live threshold has a justification you can give from memory, and the escalation and challenge routes have survived audit scrutiny
• The platform partner treats you as the decision-maker and is candid about problems rather than defensive
The perks:
It really is more than a job. We think like a start-up, but we deliver like a FTSE 100 — so thebar is high, and we won't pretend otherwise. We work hybrid, which means three days in the office. We’ll recognise your talent and make sure that you can still have a life – at work, and outside of it. Networks, committees, awards, sports and social clubs, mentorships,
volunteering opportunities, extra time off… the list goes on.
• Competitive salary
• Flexible Benefits Package on top of your salary (12%)
• Private medical cover for you and your family
• Life insurance
• Contribution to gym memberships
• 25 Days holiday, with 1 additional day off to celebrate your Birthday & 2 additional days off a year for voluntary work (28 in total)
• The option to buy or sell holiday days
• A comprehensive global and local onboarding process
• Enhanced primary (maternity), secondary (paternity), and shared parental pay and leave, as well as a range of support and benefits for parents

Overview:
At Zebra, we are a community of innovators who come together to create new ways of working. United by curiosity and a culture of caring, we develop smart solutions that anticipate our customer’s and partner’s needs and solve their challenges.
Being part of Zebra Nation means you are seen, heard, valued, and respected. Drawing from our unique perspectives, we collaborate to deliver on our purpose. Here you are part of a team pushing boundaries today to redefine the work of tomorrow for organizations, their employees, and those they serve.
You’ll have opportunities to learn and lead in a forward-thinking environment, defining your path to a fulfilling career while channeling your skills toward causes you care about—locally and globally.
Come make an impact every day at Zebra.
What We're Looking For:
We are looking for an AI Research Scientist specialising in SLAM, Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO), and 3D Spatial Perception to join our central CTO Group. In this horizontal, high-impact organisation, you will collaborate with cross-functional business units across the globe and work closely with our London-based research hub of ~15 AI specialists.
In this role, you will be bridging the gap between innovation and on-device execution -prototyping new algorithms, training spatial models, and optimising them to run directly on resource-constrained mobile edge devices to power next-generation Augmented Reality (AR), enterprise vision, and edge intelligence.
You will be based at our central London office (Endeavour House, Shaftesbury Avenue, WC2H 8JR) on a flexible hybrid model - collaborating in person 3 days a week, with 2 days working from home.
Responsibilities:
• Research, design, and implement robust Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO), 6-DoF camera pose estimation, and monocular SLAM pipelines tailored for resource-constrained edge hardware.
• Develop advanced algorithms for spatial localisation, multi-view ray triangulation, sensor fusion (IMU + Camera), and plane-fitting (e.g., RANSAC, PnP) to achieve sub-centimetre overlay accuracy and eliminate tracking drift.
• Translate research papers into real-time algorithms, optimising neural networks and spatial pipelines for low-latency execution on mobile NPUs, DSPs, and GPUs.
• Build spatial foundations that deliver seamless on-device AR experiences, barcode/shelf product recognition, OCR, and multi-modal edge AI capabilities without relying on cloud connectivity.
• Partner with global hardware, software, and product engineering teams to integrate your models into commercial product roadmaps.
Qualifications:
• Master’s or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or a related quantitative field with a specialised focus on Computer Vision, Spatial AI, or Robotics.
• At least 2 years of hands-on experience in research and development of SLAM / Spatial tracking systems.
• Deep theoretical understanding and hands-on implementation of SLAM (Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping) and VIO (Visual-Inertial Odometry).
• Strong foundation in 6-DoF pose tracking, sensor fusion (IMU + Vision), and camera calibration (intrinsic/extrinsic parameters).
• 3D geometric computer vision: ray-plane intersections, epipolar geometry, bundle adjustment, and monocular depth estimation.
• High proficiency in C++ and/or Python, along with standard ML and Computer Vision frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, OpenCV, ROS/GTSAM/Ceres Solver).
Benefits:
• 25 days of vacation
• Up to 32 hours paid time off per year to volunteer with a charity of your choice
• Reward & Recognition scheme - earn points to spend online
• Training and personal development in soft skills and hard skills, access to our internal learning portal and internal career opportunities within Zebra departments

Joining Moderna means advancing mRNA science to transform medicine. Work with exceptional global teams on a broad pipeline and build a career that makes a real difference for patients.
This is an opportunity to play a hands-on role within Moderna’s mRNA vaccine production operations at Harwell, combining scientific understanding with technical manufacturing expertise to help produce safe and effective vaccines.
As an individual contributor, you will operate production equipment in accordance with current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP), health and safety requirements, standard operating procedures and manufacturing documentation.
Working in a highly technological manufacturing environment, you will bring strong digital proficiency and a scientific approach to troubleshooting, rapidly learning new mRNA manufacturing technologies while maintaining meticulous attention to detail. You will collaborate closely with Quality Assurance and cross-functional partners to support compliant operations, timely commercial batch disposition and operational excellence, while contributing to continuous improvement, digital innovation and opportunities to engage with emerging technologies, including Generative AI tools.
Here’s What You’ll Do:
• Execute manufacturing operations in accordance with current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP), standard operating procedures and approved manufacturing documentation.
• Operate production equipment safely and effectively while adhering to Moderna’s safety procedures, guidelines and health and safety requirements.
• Follow required gowning procedures and maintain excellent housekeeping standards within assigned manufacturing areas to ensure a compliant and safe working environment.
• Proactively identify and report compliance, health and safety issues to the Team Lead or Supervisor.
• Partner closely with Quality Assurance colleagues to complete and close documentation required for the timely disposition of commercial batches.
• Participate in incident and deviation investigations, including Root Cause Analysis (RCA), and contribute to Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) activities.
• Apply established performance tools and work collaboratively with colleagues to achieve operational KPI objectives and support plans aligned with corporate goals and commercial demand.
• Respond rapidly to routine production challenges and troubleshoot equipment, process and digital issues.
• Perform routine basic equipment maintenance, including lubrication, basic mechanical checks and filter changes, using appropriate hand tools.
• Maintain training records and all associated documentation accurately and ensure they remain current.
• Participate in multiple projects and continuous improvement initiatives within a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
• Bring digital proficiency to day-to-day manufacturing operations, identifying opportunities to improve how technology and data are used within the production environment.
• Participate actively in operational improvements and innovation, including opportunities to gain exposure to emerging digital capabilities and Generative AI tools that can support manufacturing workflows, learning and operational excellence.
• Work effectively and collaboratively within a dynamic, cross-functional matrix environment, partnering fluidly with peers, leadership, Quality Assurance and other cross-functional support groups.
• Maintain meticulous attention to detail while managing multiple activities with minimal supervision.
• Demonstrate flexibility to work off-hours and overtime when required to support manufacturing operations and commercial demand.
• Bring a scientific way of thinking, strong technical capability and the ability to rapidly learn and apply new technologies associated with mRNA manufacturing.
• Contribute as a collaborative team member while operating as a hands-on individual contributor within the Harwell manufacturing organization.
The key Moderna Mindsets you’ll need to succeed in the role:
• “We obsess over learning. We don’t have to be the smartest we have to learn the fastest.”
• “We digitize everywhere possible using the power of code to maximize our impact on patients.”
Here’s What You’ll Need:
• 3+ years of experience in a GMP manufacturing environment
• A university degree with a specialization in Pharmaceutical production technology or equivalent
• Experience with filtration and chromatography, and cold chain management a plus
• Experience in audit / inspection preparation, understanding Health authority and regulatory guidelines
• Ability to collaborate fluidly with peers, leadership and cross-functional support groups required
• Excellent written, oral communication, and organizational skills required.
• Ability to maintain attention to detail while executing multiple tasks with minimal supervision
• Demonstrated commitment to Moderna's values of Bold, Collaborative, Curious, and Relentless, embodying these values in the workplace
As part of Moderna’s commitment to workplace safety, this role may require an enhanced pre-employment check.
Our Working Model
As we build our company, we have always believed that an in-person culture is critical to our success. This role is 100% onsite, reflecting the importance of being physically present to support the work, collaborate closely with colleagues, and contribute to our site-based operations.
Working onsite enables real-time collaboration, strong team connections, direct mentorship, and the hands-on partnership needed to deliver our mission. Join us in shaping a world where every interaction is an opportunity to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact.
Moderna is a smoke-free, alcohol-free, and drug-free work environment.
Pay & Benefits

CIVILS OPERATIVE
Clean Water and Wastewater Networks • Northumbrian Water
DEPARTMENT / FUNCTION Operations / Networks Delivery REPORTS TO Team Leader / Site Supervisor LOCATION Northumbrian Water operating region (North East England)
CONTRACT
Permanent • Full time HOURS 50 hours • Mon–Fri CLIENT Northumbrian Water Group (NWG)
Purpose of the role
To carry out safe, high-quality excavation, installation, repair, reinstatement and associated groundworks on Northumbrian Water clean water and wastewater assets. Working as part of a civils crew under the Team Leader, the Operative delivers planned and reactive work to Northumbrian Water specifications, street works legislation, hygiene requirements and company SHEQ procedures.
Context
Northumbrian Water supplies water and wastewater services across the North East of England. Delivery includes planned capital and maintenance work and reactive repair, often in live highways, private land and operational sites. The Civils Operative is a hands-on member of the crew, responsible for the quality of their own work, safe working around buried services, and a professional standard with customers and the public.
Key accountabilities
Civils and network operations
• Carry out excavation, trench support, pipe laying, jointing, connections, repairs and backfill on water mains, services, sewers, rising mains, chambers, manholes and associated assets.
• Install, repair and replace ironwork, covers and frames, chambers, ducting and minor civil structures to specification.
• Undertake highway and private-land reinstatement, including bituminous, concrete, flagged and landscaped finishes.
• Support mains isolations, commissioning, chlorination and hygiene arrangements in line with the Disinfection Code of Practice and clean-water protocols.
• Operate plant and equipment within competence and permit conditions, including excavator and dumper where ticketed, compaction plant and hand tools.
• Use abrasive wheels, cutting and grinding equipment only when trained and authorised.
• Locate and avoid buried services using safe digging practice and HSG47 principles, including CAT and Genny where trained.
• Identify and report defects, uncharted apparatus and network risks to the Team Leader.
• Respond to reactive and emergency work, including bursts, collapses, flooding, dangerous apparatus and out-of-hours call-out when on rota.
Health, safety, environment and quality
• Work to the safe system of work, risk assessment, method statement and permits briefed by the Team Leader.
• Help set out and maintain barriers, signing, lighting and guarding in accordance with NRSWA / Safety at Street Works and Road Works.
• Work safely in excavations and, where trained, support confined-space activities under a written safe system of work.
• Use correct manual handling techniques and mechanical aids; do not lift beyond capability.
• Protect live services, the environment and water quality; control silt, fuel, spoil and waste.
• Stop work and report immediately if conditions are unsafe, a service is struck, or a near miss occurs.
• Leave a clean, secure and compliant site at the end of each shift.
Customer and records
• Represent the company and Northumbrian Water professionally on customers’ property, in the highway and on operational sites.
• Complete personal timesheets and support site records, photographs and materials returns as directed.
• Follow instructions from the Team Leader and raise issues early if the job cannot be completed as planned.
Essential requirements
• Experience as a civils, utilities or groundworks operative, ideally on water, drainage or highway works.
• Ability to work safely as part of a small crew on live sites and in public areas.
• Valid CSCS card (or equivalent).
• Full UK driving licence; ability to travel across the Northumbrian Water region and attend standby / emergency call-out.
• Physically fit for manual work and prepared to work outdoors in all weather.
• Reliable, safety-focused and willing to work flexible hours including early starts, weekends and a standby rota.
Desirable tickets and qualifications
• NRSWA / Street Works (Operative or Supervisor as appropriate to the role)
• Confined space (City & Guilds or equivalent)
• Excavator ticket (CPCS / NPORS or equivalent)
• Dumper ticket (CPCS / NPORS or equivalent)
• Manual handling
• Abrasive wheels
• First aid
• HSG47 – Avoiding danger from underground services (CAT and Genny / service avoidance)
• EUSR National Water Hygiene / Blue Card and SHEA Water.
• Experience on Northumbrian Water or another UK water company network.
Behaviours and competencies
• Puts health, safety and water quality first and will speak up if something is wrong.
• Takes pride in workmanship and leaves sites tidy.
• Works well in a team and follows briefings without cutting corners.
• Calm and polite with customers, even on reactive or disruption-related jobs.
• Willing to learn Northumbrian Water specifications, hygiene rules and new tickets.
Working environment
The role is predominantly outdoor and physically demanding. Work takes place in live highways, excavations, operational treatment and network sites, and private property, in all weather. The post holder must be fit for manual work, prepared to work in muddy, confined or hygienically controlled conditions, and able to wear required PPE including hygiene clothing on clean-water tasks.
Additional information
A full occupational driving assessment, drugs and alcohol screening, and baseline health surveillance may be required. Training will be provided on Northumbrian Water systems, specifications and hygiene protocols where these are not already held. The employer reserves the right to amend duties in line with operational need across AMP programmes and reactive networks contracts.
This job description is not exhaustive. The post holder will be expected to undertake other reasonable duties consistent with the level and nature of the role.

NVIDIA has been redefining computer graphics and accelerated computing for three decades. Today, we are tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. Doing what has never been done before takes vision, innovation, and exceptional talent. As an NVIDIAN, you will be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is encouraged to do their best work and make a lasting impact on the world. We are looking for a Solutions Architect's to work with academia and research partners. Solutions Architects are the primary technical contacts for our customers and engage deeply with researchers and application developers to drive the adoption of NVIDIA technology. We seek an individual who combines an intricate understanding of modern AI and HPC research workloads with expertise in accelerated computing and architecture.
What you will be doing:
•
Partner directly with leading research labs, researchers, and university faculty as a trusted technical advisor: develop a keen understanding of their scientific goals and drive joint research projects at supercomputing scale.
•
Identify and accelerate high-impact workloads by integrating NVIDIA's frameworks, libraries, and core software stack into research projects, and help researchers amplify their impact through publications, conference presentations, and technical content.
•
Advocate for accelerated computing and Deep Learning, and deliver hands-on trainings, workshops, lectures, and demonstrations across NVIDIA's platforms, and mentor power users to become NVIDIA champions.
•
Track emerging research trends and turn gaps between researcher needs and NVIDIA's o erings into prototypical solutions and direct feedback to NVIDIA Engineering.
•
Maintain deep expertise in your domain while staying versatile across NVIDIA's full platform: GPUs, CPUs, networking, and software
What we need to see:
•
A graduate degree from a leading university in a STEM related discipline.
•
5+ years of hands-on experience running the large language model lifecycle across multi-node systems: training, fine-tuning, inference, serving, and/or agentic workflows.
•
Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to build relationships with academic and research stakeholders, and to communicate complex ideas clearly to both expert and non-expert audiences.
•
Action oriented, analytical, self-motivated, and a passionate learner, with excellent organization skills to work in a heavily multi-tasked environment.
•
Fluent in English, both oral and written, and comfortable working in Python.
Ways to stand out from the crowd:
•
A PhD from a leading university in a STEM related discipline, with 3+ years of research on large language models or foundation models and their applications.
•
A track record of thought leadership: high-impact publications, talks at academic conferences and workshops, as well as good understanding of scientific policy engagement, grant processes, or national/European research program structures.

Experience with NVIDIA's AI software stack, powered by CUDA and CUDA-X libraries, e.g. NVIDIA AI Enterprise, NeMo Framework, Megatron Bridge, NIM, TensorRT-LLM, Dynamo, NeMo Agent Toolkit, and Triton Inference Server, as well as the Nemotron open-model methodology.

Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Leadership and teamworking skills.

Proficiency in Microsoft Office and other relevant IT systems.

Eligibility to live and work in the United Kingdom.

Quantity tracking and installed quantity measurement on construction projects

Value engineering and feasibility study execution across labour, materials, and scope

At PwC, our people in finance consulting specialise in providing consulting services related to financial management and strategy. These individuals analyse client needs, develop financial solutions, and offer guidance and support to help clients optimise their financial performance, improve decision-making, and achieve their financial goals.
As a finance consulting generalist at PwC, you will possess a broad understanding of various aspects of finance consulting. Your work will involve providing comprehensive guidance and support to clients in optimising their financial performance, improving decision-making, and achieving their financial goals. You will be responsible for analysing client needs, developing financial solutions, and offering recommendations tailored to specific business requirements.
I&AWM Finance Solutions Director
About the role
To sustain growth and broaden the I&AWM Finance Solutions business, we are seeking an experienced Director from the external market who can lead the full client lifecycle - originating opportunities, shaping the proposition and architecture, mobilising the right capabilities across PwC, and remaining accountable through delivery and value realisation. This is a senior market-facing role for someone who creates opportunities, builds trusted relationships and converts those relationships into high-value, multi-phase transformation programmes.
The Director will act as a Finance Business Architect: understanding the client business model and strategic agenda, translating this into an integrated Finance transformation response, and connecting functional depth with controls, technology, data and AI, organisation design and service delivery. A critical part of the role is shaping how Data, AI and agentic capabilities change Finance processes, controls, roles and decision-making, working across the technology ecosystem while keeping the Finance outcome at the centre.
The role is also important to building the next generation of the team: developing people, codifying methods and assets, strengthening our Communities of Practice and ensuring our propositions and delivery capability evolve with the market.
This role demands a strong blend of commercial leadership, Finance Business Architecture, deep sector and functional expertise, Data and AI fluency, and people leadership.
What your days will look like:
• Originate, shape, sell and deliver complex Finance transformation opportunities across I&AWM, leading senior client interactions from the initial problem statement through solution architecture, mobilisation, delivery and value realisation.
• Act as a Finance Business Architect, translating enterprise strategy and the client business model into an integrated Finance target operating model spanning process, controls, technology, data and AI, organisation and workforce, and service delivery.
• Lead agentic process re-engineering across Finance: identify where AI agents, automation and human judgement should reshape end-to-end processes; define the required controls, data, roles and governance; and connect these changes into the wider enterprise architecture.
• Own the Finance Solutions demand into the Data and AI ecosystem, working with other areas of our business, hyperscalers, data platforms and frontier AI providers to develop Finance-specific propositions, reference architectures, use cases, assets and delivery patterns.
• Lead multi-tower Finance Transformation programmes across Insurance and Asset & Wealth Management, connecting R2R, P2P, O2C, Performance Management, Treasury and Tax with the wider enterprise transformation agenda.
• Bring deep understanding of insurer and asset / wealth management business models and value drivers, ensuring Finance transformation aligns to product, investments, actuarial, capital, risk, operations and technology change rather than being designed in isolation.
• Originate and expand C-suite relationships with CFOs, Finance Directors, Group Financial Controllers and transformation leaders, converting initial conversations into multi-phase, high-value programmes and new Finance Solutions revenue pools.
• Orchestrate the wider PwC ecosystem - including ERP practices, Cloud, Data & AI practices, specialist Finance technology, Workforce, Risk & Modelling and Tax - while retaining coherence of the Finance solution and accountability for the client outcome.
• Build and develop a high-performing team through coaching, sponsorship, feedback, capability development and active career support; develop future leaders and strengthen the I&AWM Finance Solutions community.
• Develop and industrialise Finance Solutions IP, including points of view, reference architectures, methods, assets and accelerators, and use these to strengthen propositions, client conversations and delivery quality.
This role is for you if:
• An established Director-calibre Finance transformation leader from the external market, with the presence and credibility to lead senior client relationships from origination through delivery and a track record of creating and converting opportunities.
• A strong Finance Business Architect who can connect strategy, business model and enterprise transformation to the detailed Finance operating model, with depth across process, controls, technology, data and AI, organisation and workforce, and service delivery.
• Demonstrable understanding and experience of Data and AI-enabled Finance transformation, including an understanding of the hyperscaler / data-platform / frontier-model ecosystem and how agentic process re-engineering changes Finance process, controls, data, roles and governance.
• Deep knowledge of Finance functional areas and the ability to work across R2R, P2P, O2C, Performance Management, Treasury and Tax, while integrating them into one coherent architecture.
• Strong sector depth across Insurance and Asset & Wealth Management, ideally with particular understanding of insurer economics, operating models and the interaction between Finance, investments, actuarial, capital, risk and operations.
• A consistent track record of shaping and leading complex, multi-tower Finance transformation programmes and delivering measurable client outcomes, with strong commercial discipline around scope, economics, risk and value.
• A proven people leader who has built teams, developed future leaders, coached and sponsored talent, and created a culture of high standards, collaboration, knowledge sharing and continuous capability development.
• A proactive growth leader with the drive to build new relationships, develop propositions, open new areas of demand and help scale Finance Solutions across I&AWM.
• Ideally combines Big Four / leading consulting experience with substantive industry experience, bringing both advisory discipline and practical understanding…

About us
Datasite is the essential infrastructure for M&A. Also comprising Grata, Blueflame AI, and Sherpany, we help dealbreakers find opportunities, manage transactions, and make key decisions.
Whatever your talents, you can find a place for them here. Get involved in some of the biggest business ventures today. Work with other gifted people around the world. Follow your ambitions, or discover a whole new path.
Can you help us simplify the complex, create great experiences, and deliver better outcomes? Then let's talk.
Job Description:
We’re not looking for someone who’s planning to try AI one day. We’re hiring someone who already uses it to prospect smarter, qualify faster, and hit the phones with more context than the competition — and who wants to keep pushing that edge at the top of the funnel.
This is a Sales Development role where you own top-of-funnel for our Deals product — the platform of choice for M&A, capital raising, insolvency, and private equity. You’ll generate and qualify pipeline across the EMEA region, working hand-in-hand with AEs, Marketing, and Digital Growth. AI is how you’ll do more of the right work, with less noise.
How AI changes this role
You don’t make cold calls. You make informed ones.
The best SDRs used to spend hours building lists, writing sequences, and manually researching prospects before every call. In this team, AI handles the heavy lifting — so you spend your time on the conversations, instincts, and follow-through that actually fill the pipeline.
Prospecting: more signal, less noise
Use AI to build targeted account lists, identify trigger events (new hires, deals announced, funding rounds), and surface the right prospects at the right moment — so your outreach lands when it matters, not at random.
Outreach: personalised at scale
AI drafts tailored email sequences, LinkedIn messages, and call scripts in minutes — personalised to each prospect’s context, industry, and pain points. You review, refine, and send. Volume without sacrificing relevance.
Call prep: walk into every conversation informed
Before every call, AI synthesises account research, recent news, and company context so you show up knowing the prospect’s world — not scrambling through tabs while you’re on hold.
Lead qualification: faster, sharper decisions
AI helps you score and prioritise inbound leads, flag high-intent signals, and surface the accounts most likely to convert — so you focus energy where it counts and hand the right opportunities to your AEs.
What you’ll do:
Generate and qualify pipeline:
• Prospect across email, phone, social, and live chat to engage and qualify new opportunities across EMEA.
• Convert inbound leads and run outbound campaigns — with AI accelerating research and personalisation at every step.
• Deliver high-quality, well-qualified opportunities to the AE team.
Support strategic accounts:
• Build awareness and relationships within focus accounts across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa — driving education and engagement ahead of buying decisions.
• Join in-person meetings with key accounts to support relationship-building and revenue growth.
• Identify expansion signals and share them with the wider pod.
Raise the bar:
• Use Salesforce to track activity, manage pipeline data, and keep everything clean and current.
• Work cross-functionally with Marketing, Digital Growth, and AEs to sharpen campaign targeting and follow-up across the region.
• Share what’s working — your sequences, your AI prompts, your call openers.
What we’re looking for
Experience Experience in a sales or client-facing role, with a strong interest in building a career in tech sales — specifically in M&A and corporate finance. You’re commercially sharp, curious about the industry, and hungry to develop fast. Fluency in English is essential; additional European languages are a strong advantage.
AI fluency:
• You use LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) daily — not occasionally.
• You prompt for real output: prospecting lists, outreach sequences, call prep, objection handling.
• You know where AI gives you an edge — and where your instincts and energy still win.
• You share what works and you’re always looking for what’s next.
Mindset:
• Hunter — you love the chase and building relationships from scratch.
• High-impact communicator — strong verbal and written skills, comfortable engaging senior stakeholders across cultures.
• AI-curious by default — always looking for a better, faster way.
• Metric-driven and outcome-focused.
• Fast learner who shares the wins (and the lessons).
Success in this role looks like:
• Pipeline → consistent volume of high-quality, well-qualified opportunities across EMEA.
• Conversion → inbound and outbound leads moving through the funnel.
• Outreach → personalised, relevant, and landing with the right people.
• Velocity → faster qualification cycles powered by sharper AI-assisted prep.

Join the team designing the future of dealmaking.
Ansarada is the secure dealmaking infrastructure company. We help companies, governments, and their advisors protect what matters and realise their potential when it counts. From M&A and capital raising to restructures, audit, and infrastructure procurement, we provide the system of record that keeps critical information secure and processes under control.
Founded in Sydney in 2005, Ansarada is trusted across 170 countries and has supported more than 55,000 transactions, bringing together data, workflow, and security by design so teams can move with clarity and confidence when the stakes are high.
Great Place to Work certified for 16 years running. Recognised as one of Australia’s Best Places to Work for Women and in Technology. Teams across Sydney, Ho Chi Minh, Chicago, Amsterdam, and London.

Senior Medical Writer
ICON is a global healthcare intelligence and clinical research organisation united by a mission to bring new medicines and treatments to patients faster.
As a values-driven organisation, integrity, collaboration, agility, and inclusion are at the heart of how we work and interact with each other, customers, patients and suppliers.
As a global provider of drug development solutions, our work is serious business. But that doesn’t mean you can’t have fun while you do it. With our vision to be the partner of choice in drug development, we hire only the best and brightest in the industry. Are you one of them?
We are looking for conscientious, resilient, and inspiring individuals to join our team. As a Senior Medical Writer (SMW), your primary responsibility will be to provide scientific and medical/clinical writing support as part of a dedicated team servicing an assigned client. While the ability to work independently is key, the SMW will work closely with the Scientific Manager (ie, Scientific Director) and other members of the client account team to help ensure the timely delivery of high-quality and scientifically/medically accurate assigned projects. As a Senior Medical Writer, your review of junior writers’ work will also be a key part of this role. Your participation in internal company initiatives, as required, offers additional potential opportunities for growth.
The Role
As a Senior Medical Writer (SMW), prior in-depth experience with background researching, developing, and writing for the diverse array of deliverables within medical publications and medical communications is expected and will be an integral foundation for this role. The SMW role will fall broadly across the following approximate allocations (individual client account teams may have, from time to time, specific needs that may alter these allocations as may be necessary/required).
The vast majority of your time will be devoted to content development and writing, from inception to delivery, including but not limited to:
• responsibility for the accurate interpretation of clinical data (e.g., from clinical study reports, safety summaries, biostatistical tables, published articles, etc), and its accurate, concise adaptation to meet assigned projects’ stated objectives
• all compliance requirements for medical publications and medical communications, as relevant and appropriate (e.g., authorship guidelines, journal requirements, client confidential materials, etc)
• representing assigned work at internal and external (client) meetings as required (e.g., project status, author interactions, client publication committee meetings, etc)
• understanding and contributing to client publication and communication plans as required (e.g., impact on project timelines, appropriate congress and journal venues for assigned client/therapy area, relevance to client drug development planning, etc)
Some of your time will provide an opportunity to assist in the management of medical writing resources, including but not limited to, responsibility for:
• monitoring and helping to manage the medical writing workload, including for junior/other writers, as required
• collaboration with the Scientific Manager (ie, Scientific Director) and account managers to help ensure adherence to agreed-upon timelines (e.g., project status reports, proactive flagging of problems, resource limitations/availability, etc)
• assisting in the onboarding and mentoring of new and junior medical writers, as required
There may be on occasion opportunity to assist the SM (SD) and/or GMC Senior Leadership in business development activities such as background research and writing support for new business proposals
What you need
• Advanced degree, preferably PhD but PharmD and MD may also be considered
• Prior relevant experience in a medical publications/medical communications agency preferred
• Minimum of 3-5 years’ experience of high-level content development; applicants with 1-2 years’ experience as a Senior Medical Writer while at a medical communications agency preferred
• Proven history of relevant high-level writing support, including: proficiency with ICMJE and GPP guidelines; ability to read, analyze, and interpret scientific and technical journal content; ability to develop and write to prescribed styles and formats
• Ability to work efficiently with network directories/databases
• Familiarity and ability to work with industry standard resources (e.g., PubMed/Medline, clinicaltrials.gov, various market intelligence/data analytic providers, etc)
• Ability to work with cross-functional teams (e.g., editorial/library services, graphics/digital services, presentations support, etc)
• Proficiency with commonly used software including but not limited to word processing (e.g., MS Word), graphics (e.g., PowerPoint or Prism), and bibliographic software (e.g., EndNote), and adaptability to other applicable software as may be required from time to time
• Experience in resource organizing and mentoring strongly preferred
• Must have demonstrable command of the English language (read, write and speak)
• A strong desire to be a key part of a global network of services that lead to better outcomes for its clients, its people and for patients…apply now and Own IT@ICON !

Do you want to help professional services firms and in-house tax teams redesign and scale how tax work gets done?

LexisNexis Legal & Professional, which serves customers in more than 150 countries with 11,800 employees worldwide, is part of RELX, a global provider of informationbased analytics and decision tools for professional and business customers. Our company has been a long-time leader in deploying AI and advanced technologies to the legal market to improve productivity and transform the overall business and practice of law, deploying ethical and powerful generative AI solutions with a flexible, multi-model approach that prioritizes using the best model from today’s top model creators for each individual legal use case. The company employs over 2,000 technologists, data scientists, and experts to develop, test, and validate solutions in line with RELX Responsible AI Principles.

• Lead customer and executive conversations that demonstrate value, build momentum and support broader adoption.
• Act as the voice of the customer, translating feedback, requirements and adoption barriers into actionable insights for Product and Development teams.
• Capture and share best practices, workflow patterns and reusable solutions across customers and internal teams.

• Professional qualification in tax or accountancy (e.g. CTA, ACA, ACCA or equivalent), ideally with 3+ years' post-qualification experience gained within a Big Four or leading mid-tier accountancy/professional services firm, or a major in-house tax team.
• Deep understanding of tax processes and workflows across one or more tax disciplines, with the ability to identify where technology and AI-enabled workflows can improve how tax work is delivered.
• Demonstrable experience of working directly with customers or senior stakeholders to drive engagement, adoption or change, with confidence influencing stakeholders up to Partner, Head of Tax or firm-owner level.
• Strong consulting, facilitation and presentation skills, with the ability to proactively lead customer conversations, uncover high-value use cases and translate business problems into practical workflow solutions.
• Commercially and outcome focused, with the ability to work against defined adoption and usage targets, use customer and product data to identify opportunities, and take ownership for progressing customers from initial engagement through to sustained workflow usage and expansion.
• Strong aptitude for tax technology, AI and workflow transformation, with practical experience using generative AI or AI-enabled tools and the ability to become highly proficient in configuring, testing and deploying AI-enabled workflows and skills using the platform.
• Excellent relationship-building and change-management skills, with the ability to mobilise different stakeholder groups within a customer organisation and help embed new ways of working into day-to-day tax practice.
• A collaborative and continuous-improvement mindset, with the ability to identify reusable workflow patterns, share best practice and translate customer feedback and adoption barriers into actionable insights for Product and Development teams.
Success in this Role
Success in this role is measured by the adoption and sustained use of Tolley+ Protégé and workflows across customer organisations.
Successful Tax Engineers consistently engage priority customers, enable workflow capabilities within customer accounts, identify and deploy high-value workflows, and increase their active usage of Tolley+ Protégé across relevant teams and tax disciplines.
They are able to take an ambiguous or manual tax process, understand how it works, turn it into a practical AI-enabled workflow, and see that workflow adopted and delivering measurable value in a real customer environment.

Quantitative Researcher
CMC Markets strives to provide the best trading experience for a wide spectrum of clients to participate in the financial markets. In order to expand this team, we are looking for an experienced Quantitative Researcher to coach and mentor others whilst contributing fully towards our shared goals.
Our Quants have responsibility for pricing models covering an expanding product range and also work to optimise CMC’s risk management strategies.
This role will offer a varied and fast-paced working environment, regularly interacting with the dealing, operations, risk and IT development teams. This is an excellent opportunity to be sitting in the core of the business and develop a deep understanding of the Market Making financial industry.
Key responsibilities:
• Coach, mentor and help grow an existing team of Quantitative Researchers.
• Conduct research into alpha opportunities, pricing improvements, hedging effectiveness and execution performance across CMC's product set.
• Research, develop and deploy machine learning and AI models to improve pricing, forecasting, risk management and trading decision-making across the business.
• Partner with developers and trading stakeholders to productionise research outputs and monitor model performance after deployment.
• Translate complex analytical findings into clear recommendations for both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Maintain personal/professional development to meet the changing demands of the role, including all relevant regulatory and legislative training.
• Take all reasonable steps to ensure appropriate confidentiality.
Key skills & experience:
• A degree in quantitative finance, mathematics, computer science or equivalent disciplines.
• Strong analytical and quantitative research capabilities, ideally gained in trading, market making, electronic execution, derivatives or other front-office environments.
• Experience applying machine learning and AI techniques to financial and time-series data, including feature engineering, model selection, validation and performance monitoring.
• Strong skills in Python, SQL and time-series analysis.
• Experience using Python ML libraries such as scikit-learn, XGBoost, PyTorch or TensorFlow.
• Experience analysing high-volume or high-frequency time-series data and building reliable research workflows.
• Ability to design robust experiments and evaluate models using appropriate metrics, cross-validation and out-of-sample testing.
• Understanding of model governance, explainability, bias, overfitting and production monitoring in a regulated environment.
• Excellent communication skills, both written and spoken.

For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.  Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.
For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vetting

The Flow Laboratory Analyst is responsible for conducting advanced and routine analytical testing to ensure the quality and integrity of products and processes. The role involves performing laboratory testing on geological, fluid, and gas samples, operating and maintaining specialised equipment, reviewing and reporting data, and ensuring compliance with quality, safety, and environmental standards. • Operate, calibrate, maintain, and troubleshoot laboratory equipment and instrumentation in accordance with established procedures and industry standards.
• Accurately record, analyse, review, and report test results, ensuring data quality, integrity, and compliance with required specifications.
• Complete all laboratory worksheets, data forms, records, reports, and administrative documentation accurately and within required timescales.
• Maintain a clean, organised, and safe working environment, ensuring laboratory housekeeping standards are consistently met.
• Adhere to company quality, health, safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements, including ISO Quality Management Systems and QA/QC procedures.
• Identify, report, and where appropriate intervene to prevent unsafe, environmentally irresponsible, or non-compliant practices.
• Report non-conformances and participate in corrective and preventive action processes to support continuous improvement.
• Collaborate with colleagues and other departments to ensure efficient operations, effective communication, and consistency of data and service delivery.
• Support the training and development of colleagues and contribute to the sharing of technical knowledge and best practices.
• Respect and protect Company and client confidentiality at all times.
• Travel domestically or internationally, including offshore assignments, as required to support operational needs.
• Perform additional duties as assigned, demonstrating adaptability and a commitment to operational excellence.
QUALIFICATIONS
• Relevant laboratory experience, including exposure to analytical testing and data processing.
